https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.title: NNPC Cuts Exploration Spending by 87%, Gas Flare Bill Falls to N499bn
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.summary: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) slashed additions to its exploration and evaluation assets by 87.7 per cent to N78.8 billion in 2025, from N640.5 billion in 2024, according to its latest Annual Financial Report (AFS).
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.summary_zh: 尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司（NNPC）将其勘探和评估资产的增加额削减87.7%至2025年的788亿奈拉，2024年为6405亿奈拉，根据其最新的年度财务报告（AFS）。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.body: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) slashed additions to its exploration and evaluation assets by 87.7 per cent to N78.8 billion in 2025, from N640.5 billion in 2024, according to its latest Annual Financial Report (AFS). In the same vein, the national oil company’s gas flaring charges during the period under consideration fell by 62.2 per cent from N1.32 trillion in 2024 to N499 billion in 2025, the financial report indicated. However, the decline in exploration funding may not be unconnected with the slowdown in the search for hydrocarbons in underexplored areas, including the Chad Basin, Benue Trough, Bida Basin and Sokoto Basin, all in the northern part of Nigeria. Despite billions of naira committed to the programme, projects such as Kolmani, straddling Bauchi and Gombe states; drilling and appraisal activities such as the Wadi-2 exploratory well in Borno and exploration activities and seismic data gathering in Nasarawa state have yet to reach breakthrough levels. To compound the matter. President Bola Tinubu’s Executive Order 9 of 2026, has now suspended NNPC’s collection and management of the 30 per cent Frontier Exploration Fund (FEF) and ordered that the money be remitted directly to the Federation Account for distribution among the federal, state and local governments. On gas flaring, the group’s total charges declined to N499 billion from N1.32 trillion in 2024. The amount comprised N247.8 billion in flare fees, down from N708.6 billion, and N251.2 billion in penalties for flaring above approved limits, compared with N610.4 billion previously. The fees are statutory charges based on limits approved by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) under Section 104 of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA). Despite the reduction, penalties accounted for approximately half of the group’s total gas flaring charges. At the parent company level, gas flaring charges dropped to N317.3 billion from N1.04 trillion. The decline came as NNPC paid N11.56 trillion to settle royalties, rentals and gas flare obligations during the year, more than four times the N2.83 trillion recorded in 2024. The reduction in outstanding liabilities also reflected a N1.18 trillion write-back of excess provisions from earlier years. Consequently, the group’s outstanding liability under the category fell by 86.2 per cent to N1.27 trillion from N9.21 trillion. Royalty charges, however, increased by 4.1 per cent to N4.66 trillion, while the levy payable to the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) rose by 29.2 per cent to N514.7 billion. Overall, total additions across intangible asset classes fell by 88.6 per cent to N79 billion, from N692.7 billion in 2024, while additions to mineral rights were nil, compared with N46.3 billion a year earlier. Mineral rights represent rights associated with exploring for or extracting oil and gas from specified acreage. In Nigeria’s petroleum industry, these rights are linked to legally recognised entitlements to undertake petroleum operations, subject to applicable laws, lease terms and regulatory approvals. The absence of additions means NNPC recorded no new expenditure in that asset category during the year. The report also showed that mineral rights valued at N16.4 billion relating to oil mining leases 64 and 66 were removed after being fully impaired. An impairment occurs when an asset’s recorded value is no longer considered recoverable under applicable accounting rules. The report also disclosed lower spending on selected operational activities, as rig site and stimulation expenses declined to N2.9 billion from N16.5 billion earlier recorded by the national oil company. Besides, the AFS showed that allocated technical and production costs fell to N144.4 billion from N489.6 billion, while crude handling and port charges declined to N1.06 trillion from N1.52 trillion.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.title_zh: NNPC将勘探支出削减87%，天然气燃烧账单降至N499bn
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.body_zh: 尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司（NNPC）将其勘探和评价资产的增量削减了87.7%，从2024年的N640.5 billion降至2025年的N78.8 billion，根据其最新的年度财务报告（AFS）。同样，国家石油公司在所考虑期间的气体燃烧费用下降了62.2%，从2024年的N1.32 trillion降至2025年的N499 billion，该财务报告显示。然而，勘探资金的下降可能与在未充分勘探地区寻找碳氢化合物的放缓有关，包括乍得盆地、贝努埃槽谷、比达盆地和索科托盆地，这些地区均位于尼日利亚北部。尽管该计划投入了数十亿奈拉，但诸如横跨包奇州和贡贝州的Kolmani等项目；在博尔诺州的Wadi-2勘探井等钻探和评估活动以及在纳萨拉瓦州的勘探活动和地震数据收集尚未达到突破水平。更糟糕的是，博拉·蒂努布总统2026年的第9号行政命令现已暂停NNPC对30%的边境勘探基金（FEF）的收取和管理，并命令将资金直接汇入联邦账户，以便在联邦、州和地方政府之间分配。在气体燃烧方面，该集团的总费用从2024年的N1.32 trillion下降至N499 billion。该金额包括N247.8 billion的燃烧费，从N708.6 billion下降，以及N251.2 billion的超过批准限额燃烧的罚款，而之前为N610.4 billion。这些费用是基于尼日利亚上游石油监管委员会（NUPRC）根据石油工业法（PIA）第104条批准的限额的法定费用。尽管有所减少，但罚款约占该集团气体燃烧总费用的近一半。在母公司层面，气体燃烧费用从N1.04 trillion降至N317.3 billion。这种下降是因为NNPC在当年支付了N11.56 trillion来结算特许权使用费、租金和气体燃烧义务，是2024年记录的N2.83 trillion的四倍多。未清偿负债的减少还反映了从早期年度超额准备金中转回的N1.18 trillion。因此，该集团该类别下的未清偿负债下降了86.2%，从N9.21 trillion降至N1.27 trillion。然而，特许权使用费增加了4.1%至N4.66 trillion，而应付给尼日尔三角洲发展委员会（NDDC）的征费增加了29.2%至N514.7 billion。总体而言，无形资产类别的总增量下降了88.6%，从2024年的N692.7 billion降至N79 billion，而矿产权的增量为零，而前一年为N46.3 billion。矿产权代表与在指定区域勘探或开采石油和天然气相关的权利。在尼日利亚石油工业中，这些权利与依法认可的从事石油作业的权利相关，须遵守适用的法律、租赁条款和监管批准。没有增量意味着NNPC在当年该资产类别中没有记录新的支出。该报告还显示，与石油采矿租约64和66相关的价值N16.4 billion的矿产权在完全减值后被移除。当资产的记录价值根据适用的会计规则不再被视为可收回时，就会发生减值。该报告还披露了对选定运营活动的较低支出，因为钻井现场和刺激费用从国家石油公司之前记录的N16.5 billion降至N2.9 billion。此外，AFS显示分配的技术和生产成本从N489.6 billion降至N144.4 billion，而原油处理和港口费用从N1.52 trillion降至N1.06 trillion。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.summary: The Chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), Dr. Musiliu Oseni, has called for greater collaboration and stronger cybersecurity compliance across the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry (NESI). Speaking at a cybersecurity awareness seminar, Oseni, represented by the Vice Chairman of NERC, Dr. Yusuf Ali, emphasised that the increasing digitisation of electricity infrastructure has made cybersecurity a critical component of power sector operations and national development.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.summary_zh: 尼日利亚电力监管委员会（NERC）主席穆西利乌·奥塞尼博士呼吁在尼日利亚电力供应行业（NESI）加强合作和更严格的网络安全合规。在一次网络安全意识研讨会上，由NERC副主席优素福·阿里博士代表的奥塞尼强调，电力基础设施日益数字化已使网络安全成为电力部门运营和国家发展的关键组成部分。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.body: The Chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), Dr. Musiliu Oseni, has called for greater collaboration and stronger cybersecurity compliance across the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry (NESI). He warned that cyber threats have evolved beyond the financial sector and now pose significant risks to the power sector globally. Speaking at a cybersecurity awareness seminar, Oseni, represented by the Vice Chairman of NERC, Dr. Yusuf Ali, emphasised that the increasing digitisation of electricity infrastructure has made cybersecurity a critical component of power sector operations and national development. “Cybersecurity threats are no longer confined to the financial sector alone. They have become a major concern for the electricity sector and continue to expand globally. We are only as strong as our weakest point because a cyberattack does not need to target a major node before it affects the entire system,” he stated. He stressed that the interconnected nature of power systems requires all stakeholders to take deliberate steps toward improving cybersecurity compliance and strengthening sector-wide resilience. “For Nigeria, the stakes are particularly high as we strive to achieve reliable and sustainable electricity supply. Cyber resilience can no longer be viewed solely as an ICT issue; it must be integrated into every aspect of business operations and strategic decision-making within the power sector,” he said. Oseni also highlighted the need to consider the establishment of a sector-wide emergency cyber response mechanism to enhance preparedness, facilitate rapid incident response, and promote information sharing among industry players. The seminar featured expert presentations on critical cybersecurity issues. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.body_zh: 尼日利亚电力监管委员会（NERC）主席穆西利乌·奥塞尼博士呼吁在尼日利亚电力供应行业（NESI）加强协作和强化网络安全合规。他警告称，网络威胁已超出金融部门，现在对全球电力部门构成重大风险。在一次网络安全意识研讨会上，由NERC副主席优素福·阿里博士代表的奥塞尼强调，电力基础设施日益数字化已使网络安全成为电力部门运营和国家发展的关键组成部分。“网络安全威胁不再仅限于金融部门。它们已成为电力部门的主要关切，并继续在全球范围内扩大。我们只和最薄弱的环节一样强大，因为网络攻击不需要针对主要节点就能影响整个系统，”他表示。他强调，电力系统的互联性质要求所有利益相关者采取有意识的步骤来改善网络安全合规并加强整个行业的韧性。“对尼日利亚而言，在我们努力实现可靠和可持续电力供应的过程中，风险特别高。网络韧性不能再仅仅被视为一个信息通信技术问题；它必须融入电力部门业务运营和战略决策的各个方面，”他说。奥塞尼还强调需要考虑建立一个全行业紧急网络响应机制，以提高 preparedness，促进快速事件响应，并促进行业参与者之间的信息共享。研讨会就关键网络安全问题进行了专家演讲。THISDAY 成立于 1995 年 1 月 22 日，由 THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD. 出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路 35 号，在尼日利亚 36 个州、联邦首都区和世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，可在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术与有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真理和理性，涵盖从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列问题。您可以通过 hello@thisdaylive.com 给我们发邮件或访问我们的联系页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/s.body: The President of the Surveyors Council of Nigeria (SURCON), Moshood Akinwande, has reaffirmed that the regulation of the surveying profession in Nigeria is governed by federal legislation, emphasising that the Council is the statutory body vested with the responsibility of registering surveyors and regulating the practice of the surveying profession throughout the Federation. He made the clarification in Abeokuta, Ogun State, during his two-day official working visit to the state, at the invitation of the Chairman of the Nigerian Institution of Surveyors (NIS), Ogun State Branch, Surveyor Abiodun Liadi. Speaking during the visit, the SURCON President explained that the regulation of the surveying profession falls within the legislative competence of the Federal Government, through an Act of the National Assembly. He stressed that SURCON is statutorily empowered to register qualified surveyors, regulate professional practice nationwide, and exercise disciplinary control over practitioners who contravene established professional standards. He further clarified that the Council’s regulatory authority extends to the surveying profession in all its branches and ramifications, across the 36 states of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja. Akinwande emphasised that the Council’s statutory mandate is to ensure professional competence, ethical conduct and compliance with applicable federal legislation and professional standards throughout Nigeria. He also advised members of the public, particularly prospective land purchasers, property developers and investors, to engage the services of duly registered surveyors when acquiring landed properties or undertaking survey-related transactions. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/f.summary_zh: 哈尔巴食品公司正通过以可负担性、高效制造、可扩展运营和区域贸易为中心的经济生产策略，定位于为尼日利亚食品加工行业做出贡献。哈尔巴稻米加工厂有限公司总经理哈利法·巴拉·拉比乌在谈到公司业务计划时表示，该公司打算开发一种商业模式，使不同收入水平的消费者都能获得基本食品，同时将其足迹扩展到整个西非。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/f.body: Halba Foods is positioning to contribute to Nigeria’s food processing industry through an economic production strategy centred on affordability, efficient manufacturing, scalable operations and regional trade. The Managing Director of Halba Rice Mills Ltd, Halifa Bala Rabiu, who spoke on the company’s business plans, said the company intends to develop a business model that makes essential food items accessible to consumers across different income levels while expanding its footprint across West Africa. Rabiu said Halba Rice Mills seeks to address one of the challenges facing consumers in the food market; difficulty of purchasing essential commodities in large quantities due to limited purchasing power. “We want to come up with something new by making these items very affordable in a way that everyone can afford,” Rabiu said, explaining that the strategy would focus on providing rice and edible oil in smaller package sizes. Rather than concentrating solely on the conventional 50-kilogramme and 25-kilogramme rice bags, the company plans to introduce smaller options, including one-kilogramme and 500-gramme packs. He added that a similar approach would be adopted for edible oil, with the aim of making smaller quantities available to consumers who cannot afford to purchase larger volumes at once. Rabiu noted that affordability involves more than reducing prices; it also requires making products accessible to households and lower-income consumers who need to buy essential food items in quantities that match their immediate financial capacity. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/f.body_zh: Halba Foods 正通过以可负担性、高效制造、可扩展运营和区域贸易为核心的经济生产策略，定位于为尼日利亚食品加工行业做出贡献。Halba Rice Mills Ltd 总经理 Halifa Bala Rabiu 在谈到公司业务计划时表示，公司打算开发一种商业模式，使不同收入水平的消费者都能获得基本食品，同时扩大其在西非的足迹。Rabiu 表示，Halba Rice Mills 寻求解决食品市场消费者面临的一个挑战，即由于购买力有限，难以大量购买基本商品。“我们想推出一些新东西，通过让这些商品非常实惠，让每个人都能负担得起，”Rabiu 说，并解释说该策略将侧重于提供更小包装的米和食用油。该公司没有仅仅专注于传统的50公斤和25公斤大米袋，而是计划推出更小的选项，包括1公斤和500克包装。他补充说，对食用油也将采用类似方法，目的是让无法一次性购买大包装的消费者获得更小的数量。Rabiu 指出，可负担性不仅仅涉及降低价格；它还要求让产品能够被家庭和低收入消费者获得，他们需要按照自己当前的财务能力购买基本食品。THISDAY 成立于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都区和世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术与有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真相和理性，涵盖从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列问题。您可以通过 hello@thisdaylive.com 与我们联系，或访问我们的联系页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/f.body: The federal government has pledged to intensify efforts to promote Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) as a cheaper alternative fuel for transportation, with a renewed focus on accelerating the rollout of 1 million CNG-powered vehicles across the country. To this end, the Minister of State Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, has tasked the leadership of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV) and the Decade of Gas Secretariat to focus on critical interventions. In a statement in Abuja, the minister urged the Pi-CNG & EV office and the secretariat to step up investments, expand CNG infrastructure and strengthen programmes to drive nationwide adoption. Ekpo gave the directive in Abuja while receiving progress updates from the two bodies, stressing the need to translate the federal government’s auto CNG policy into tangible benefits for Nigerians in the form of cheaper transport fares. He said the drive had become imperative following the removal of petrol subsidy and the need to provide Nigerians with a more affordable and environmentally friendly alternative for transportation, in line with the aspirations of President Bola Tinubu. In his remarks, the Executive Chairman/CEO of Pi-CNG & EV, Mr. Ismaeel Ahmed, said the initiative would step up investments and programmes to expand CNG infrastructure and increase vehicle conversions nationwide and lead to cheaper transport fares for millions of Nigerians. Ahmed explained that the joint industry market study completed by the decade of gas secretariat provided a framework for accelerating rollout, tracking progress, identifying gaps and strengthening implementation efforts to accelerate the adoption of CNG as a transportation fuel. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/f.body_zh: 联邦政府已承诺加大力度推广压缩天然气（CNG）作为交通领域更廉价的替代燃料，并重新重点加快在全国推广100万辆CNG动力汽车。为此，石油资源国务部长（天然气）埃克佩里克佩·埃克波已责成总统压缩天然气和电动汽车倡议（Pi-CNG & EV）领导层以及天然气十年秘书处专注于关键干预措施。在阿布贾发表的一份声明中，部长敦促Pi-CNG & EV办公室和秘书处加大投资、扩大CNG基础设施并加强推动全国采用的方案。埃克波在阿布贾接收这两个机构进展更新时下达了这一指示，强调需要将联邦政府的汽车CNG政策转化为尼日利亚人的切实利益，即更便宜的交通费用。他说，在取消汽油补贴之后，这一举措变得势在必行，需要为尼日利亚人提供更负担得起且环境友好的交通替代方案，这符合总统博拉·蒂努布的愿景。在他的讲话中，Pi-CNG & EV执行主席兼首席执行官伊斯梅尔·艾哈迈德先生表示，该倡议将加大投资和方案力度，以扩大CNG基础设施并增加全国车辆改装，从而为数百万尼日利亚人带来更便宜的交通费用。艾哈迈德解释说，由天然气十年秘书处完成联合行业市场研究为加快推广、跟踪进展、找出差距和加强实施工作提供了框架，以加速采用CNG作为交通燃料。THISDAY成立于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都特区及世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术与有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真相和理性，涵盖从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育、社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列问题。您可以通过hello@thisdaylive.com与我们联系，或访问我们的联系页面。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/isaac-opoku-.summary: Ghanaian youth leader Isaac Opoku has been received by the Ghana High Commissioner to the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth Secretary General in London, as he celebrates being named one of the QECT 100 Young Leaders 2026. Isaac, founder of the Starlight Foundation, visited Her Excellency Mrs Sabah Zita Benson, Ghana’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, and Her Excellency Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, Secretary-General of the Commonwealth, alongside two fellow Ghanaian awardees.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/isaac-opoku-.summary_zh: 加纳青年领袖伊萨克·奥波库在伦敦受到了加纳驻英国高级专员和英联邦秘书长接见，同时庆祝他被评为QECT 100位2026年青年领袖之一。伊萨克是星光基金会的创始人，与两名同为加纳获奖者的伙伴一起拜访了加纳驻英国高级专员萨巴赫·齐塔·本森阁下和英联邦秘书长雪莉·阿约尔科·博奇韦阁下。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/isaac-opoku-.body: Ghanaian youth leader Isaac Opoku has been received by the Ghana High Commissioner to the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth Secretary General in London, as he celebrates being named one of the QECT 100 Young Leaders 2026. Isaac, founder of the Starlight Foundation, visited Her Excellency Mrs Sabah Zita Benson, Ghana’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, and Her Excellency Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, Secretary-General of the Commonwealth, alongside two fellow Ghanaian awardees. During the visit, he shared his personal story, explained why he started the Foundation, and spoke about its work with children and families across Ghana. The three young leaders also presented the award plaques they had received. The High Commissioner said she was impressed by their work and proud that they had raised the flag of Ghana high within the Commonwealth. Madam Botchwey, the first Ghanaian and the first African woman to serve as Commonwealth Secretary-General, spoke of her pride in seeing young Ghanaians recognised at this level and of her belief in the work they are doing. “To sit before two Ghanaian women leading at the very top and hear them say they are proud of us was something I will carry for a long time,” Isaac said. “This award is for every child in Ghana who has been told their dreams are too big.” The QECT 100 Young Leaders Award, given by the Queen Elizabeth II Commonwealth Trust, marks what would have been the 100th birthday of the late Queen Elizabeth II. Isaac was first named an awardee on 21 April 2026 and received the award in person this October at a ceremony at Asprey in Mayfair, London. As an awardee, he was also invited to a reception at St James's Palace, where he spoke with His Majesty King Charles III and Her Majesty Queen Camilla, and met Her Royal Highness The Duchess of Gloucester. For Isaac, the recognition goes back to where it all began. Born and raised in Accra by a single mother, he founded the Starlight Foundation in 2018 to support children living and working on the streets and their families. Through more than 50 initiatives, the Foundation has since reached over 40,000 people. Its Centre for Design and Innovation in Accra offers a STEAM model built for vulnerable communities, and its learning resources on menstrual hygiene, personal safety, digital literacy and children's rights are now used in schools across Ghana. Its flagship programme, Menso Meka Ho Bi, meaning “I'm also privileged”, works with whole families so that children are not supported in isolation but within homes that can sustain their progress. The Foundation also contributed to the United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child's General Comment 27, giving Ghanaian voices a part in shaping global children's rights policy. This year, at the invitation of the National Youth Authority, it submitted written input to Ghana's first National Action Plan on Youth, Peace and Security. The QECT honour adds to a growing list of recognition for Isaac and the Starlight Foundation. In 2023, Isaac was named Man of Excellence in Philanthropy at the Ghana Business and Entrepreneurs Awards. In 2024, he received the Bright Futures Award for Community Impact and was named Young Philanthropist of the Year by Humanitarian Awards Global. The Starlight Foundation was named Leading Youth-Led Education NGO 2025 by Acquisition International in the UK, and this year it was named Best Child Welfare & Empowerment NPO 2026 – Ghana at the 9th annual African Excellence Awards by AI Global Media, also in the UK. The Foundation’s Let Her Know initiative has been nominated by the Ghana National Commission for UNESCO for the 2026 UNESCO Prize for Girls’ and Women’s Education. In addition, Starlight has received approval from the YOUNGO LCOY Working Group to host a Local Conference of Youth (LCOY) in Ghana in 2026, joining a global network of youth-led climate conferences recognised under the YOUNGO framework under the United Nations.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/isaac-opoku-.title_zh: Isaac Opoku在伦敦以英联邦荣誉高举加纳国旗
https://www.myjoyonline.com/isaac-opoku-.body_zh: 加纳青年领袖艾萨克·奥普库在伦敦受到了加纳驻英国高级专员和英联邦秘书长接见，他正在庆祝自己被评为QECT 100位2026年青年领袖之一。艾萨克是星光基金会的创始人，他与另外两名加纳获奖者一起拜访了加纳驻英国高级专员萨巴赫·齐塔·本森阁下和英联邦秘书长雪莉·阿约尔科·博奇韦阁下。在访问期间，他分享了自己的个人故事，解释了他为什么创立基金会，并谈到了基金会与加纳各地儿童和家庭开展的工作。三位青年领袖还展示了他们获得的奖牌。高级专员表示，她对他们的工作印象深刻，并为他们在英联邦内高高举起加纳的旗帜感到自豪。博奇韦女士作为首位担任英联邦秘书长的加纳人和非洲女性，谈到了看到加纳青年在这一层面获得认可时的自豪感，以及她对他们正在从事的工作的信念。“坐在两位处于最高领导位置的加纳女性面前，听她们说为我们感到骄傲，这是我将铭记很久的事情，”艾萨克说。“这个奖项是颁给加纳每一个被告知梦想太大的孩子的。”QECT 100位青年领袖奖由伊丽莎白二世英联邦信托基金颁发，标志着已故伊丽莎白二世女王本该迎来的100岁诞辰。艾萨克于2026年4月21日首次被提名为获奖者，并于今年10月在伦敦梅费尔Asprey举行的仪式上亲自领奖。作为获奖者，他还受邀参加在圣詹姆斯宫举行的招待会，在那里他与国王查尔斯三世陛下和卡米拉王后陛下交谈，并会见了格洛斯特公爵夫人殿下。对艾萨克来说，这一认可回到了这一切开始的地方。他在阿克拉由单亲母亲抚养长大，于2018年创立星光基金会，以支持生活在街头和工作的儿童及其家庭。通过50多项举措，该基金会此后已惠及超过4万人。其位于阿克拉的设计与创新中心为弱势社区提供了一种STEAM模式，其关于经期卫生、个人安全、数字素养和儿童权利的学习资源目前在加纳各地的学校中使用。其旗舰项目Menso Meka Ho Bi，意思是“我也有特权”，与整个家庭合作，这样儿童就不会孤立地得到支持，而是在能够维持其进步的家庭中得到支持。该基金会还为联合国儿童权利委员会第27号一般性意见做出了贡献，让加纳的声音参与塑造全球儿童权利政策。今年，应国家青年局邀请，它向加纳首份《青年、和平与安全国家行动计划》提交了书面意见。QECT的荣誉为艾萨克和星光基金会不断增加的认可名单增添了新成员。2023年，艾萨克在加纳商业与企业家奖上被评为慈善卓越人物。2024年，他获得社区影响光明未来奖，并被全球人道主义奖评为年度青年慈善家。星光基金会被英国Acquisition International评为2025年领先青年领导教育非政府组织，今年在英国AI Global Media主办的第九届非洲卓越奖上被评为2026年加纳最佳儿童福利与赋权非营利组织。该基金会的Let Her Know倡议已被加纳国家教科文组织委员会提名角逐2026年联合国教科文组织女童和妇女教育奖。此外，星光基金会已获得YOUNGO LCOY工作组批准，将于2026年在加纳主办一次青年地方会议（LCOY），加入联合国YOUNGO框架下获得认可的全球青年主导气候会议网络。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/an-unaccepta.summary: NPP National Women’s Organiser has warned that school authorities’ alleged failure to act on sexual abuse complaints at Obuasi Senior High Technical School would amount to “an unacceptable breach” of their responsibility to protect students, if established. In a statement issued on Monday, Mavis Hawa Koomson demanded an independent criminal investigation into allegations involving the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/an-unaccepta.summary_zh: 国家爱国党全国妇女组织者警告称，如果奥布阿西高级技术学校校方被证实未能对性虐待投诉采取行动，将构成对其保护学生责任的“不可接受的违反”。周一发表的一份声明中，Mavis Hawa Koomson 要求对涉及学校校长 Zakaria Abdulai 的指控进行独立的刑事调查。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/an-unaccepta.body: NPP National Women’s Organiser has warned that school authorities’ alleged failure to act on sexual abuse complaints at Obuasi Senior High Technical School would amount to “an unacceptable breach” of their responsibility to protect students, if established. In a statement issued on Monday, Mavis Hawa Koomson demanded an independent criminal investigation into allegations involving the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. Her intervention follows media reports, including an investigation by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, concerning approximately 19 female students. According to her statement, the students have recounted alleged rape, sexual harassment, sexual assault and other forms of abuse. Ms Koomson expressed particular concern over reports that some complaints reached school authorities as far back as March 2026. She said the alleged absence of meaningful action had left serious questions about the protection of affected students. If established, she said, such inaction would constitute grave negligence of the school authorities’ duty of care. She called on the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service to conduct a swift, thorough, independent and transparent investigation. Where sufficient evidence is established, she urged prosecutorial authorities to pursue legal processes regardless of the political affiliation, social standing or institutional position of anyone implicated. “A child knows no political party colours. We must never subordinate the dignity, safety, and protection of our children to partisan considerations.” Ms Koomson also raised concerns about reports of possible intimidation, victimisation and reprisals against affected students and their families. She demanded measures to protect their identities, guarantee their safety and shield those reporting alleged abuse from retaliation. She asked the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection and the Ghana Education Service to coordinate counselling, psychological support, medical care and other protective assistance. Beyond the investigation, she called for a comprehensive GES review of child protection policies and rules governing the conduct of teachers, headmasters and school administrators. She also appealed to women across the country, particularly the Vice President, to support efforts to secure justice and strengthen safeguards for girls. “Justice must be pursued without fear or favour. Accountability must know no political boundaries, and the protection of our children must remain a shared national responsibility.”
https://www.myjoyonline.com/an-unaccepta.title_zh: ‘不可接受的违规’——Hawa Koomson就奥布阿西SHTS虐待投诉据称未采取行动发出警告
https://www.myjoyonline.com/an-unaccepta.body_zh: 国家人民党全国妇女组织者警告称，如果奥布阿西高级技术学校校方被证实未能对性虐待投诉采取行动，将构成对其保护学生责任的“不可接受的违反”。周一发表的一份声明中，Mavis Hawa Koomson 要求对涉及学校校长 Zakaria Abdulai 的指控进行独立的刑事调查。她的介入是在媒体报道之后，包括记者 Manasseh Azure Awuni 的调查，涉及大约 19 名女学生。根据她的声明，这些学生讲述了所谓的强奸、性骚扰、性侵犯和其他形式的虐待。Koomson 女士对一些投诉早在 2026 年 3 月就已到达学校当局的报道表示特别关注。她说，所谓的缺乏有意义行动的情况，对受影响学生的保护提出了严重疑问。她说，如果情况属实，这种不作为将构成学校当局严重疏忽其照顾职责。她呼吁加纳警察局刑事调查部进行迅速、彻底、独立和透明的调查。在确立足够证据的情况下，她敦促检察当局无论涉案人员的党派归属、社会地位或机构职位如何，都要推进法律程序。“孩子不认识任何政党的颜色。我们绝不能将我们孩子的尊严、安全和保护置于党派考虑之下。”Koomson 女士还对可能对受影响学生及其家人进行恐吓、受害化和报复的报道表示担忧。她要求采取措施保护他们的身份、保证他们的安全，并保护那些报告所谓虐待的人免受报复。她要求性别、儿童和社会保护部以及加纳教育服务局协调提供咨询、心理支持、医疗护理和其他保护援助。除了调查之外，她呼吁加纳教育服务局全面审查儿童保护政策以及规范教师、校长和学校管理人员行为的规则。她还呼吁全国各地的妇女，特别是副总统，支持为确保正义和加强女孩保障所做的努力。“必须毫无畏惧或偏袒地追求正义。问责制必须不分政治界限，而保护我们的孩子必须始终是共同的国家责任。”

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/j.title: Japheth Njoku: When a Death in Police Custody Becomes a Test of the Rule of Law
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/j.summary: The importance of the decision goes far beyond Japheth Njoku. A person does not have to die directly from a Police bullet or a blow from an officer, before the State can bear responsibility for a death in custody. Police custody must never become a place, where illness is ignored until it becomes fatal.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/j.summary_zh: 这一决定的重要性远远超出杰费斯·恩乔库。一个人不必直接死于警察的子弹或警官的殴打，国家才能对拘留期间的死亡承担责任。警察拘留绝不能成为一个忽视疾病直到它变得致命的地方。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/j.body: J apheth Njoku entered Police custody alive. He did not leave alive. He was 32 years old when he died, after weeks in detention at the Anti-Kidnapping Unit of the Imo State Police Command, popularly known as Tiger Base, Owerri. For his family, the tragedy did not end with his death. They had to begin another struggle: to establish how he died, secure an autopsy, protect potential witnesses, and overcome repeated obstacles placed in the path of a judicial inquiry. More than a year later, the Chief Magistrate’s Court in Owerri, sitting as Coroner, has delivered findings that deserve national attention. The importance of the decision goes far beyond Japheth Njoku. It raises fundamental questions about what happens when citizens disappear behind the walls of Police detention facilities, and the enormous difficulties families face when they try to hold the State accountable. According to reports of the Coroner’s findings, Njoku was detained for approximately six weeks, over an allegation of stealing – an ordinarily bailable offence. The Coroner found that money was demanded in connection with his release and rejected attempts to justify his continued detention, by subsequently portraying him as a terrorist. The court reportedly found conditions at Tiger Base inconsistent with the rights of detainees to dignity, liberty, legal representation and bail, and identified practices involving torture, intimidation and extortion. Although the medical evidence reportedly identified meningitis, bronchial pneumonia and hypertensive heart disease among the causes of death, the Coroner made an extremely important finding: the conditions under which Njoku was detained and the length of his detention, contributed to the deterioration of his health and eventual death. That distinction matters. A person does not have to die directly from a Police bullet or a blow from an officer, before the State can bear responsibility for a death in custody. Once the State deprives a person of liberty, it assumes an enhanced duty to protect that person’s life, health and physical integrity. Police custody must never become a place, where illness is ignored until it becomes fatal. Perhaps, one of the most troubling aspects of the Njoku case, is what happened after his death. On June 11, 2025, the Coroner ordered an autopsy, and provided for an independent pathologist nominated by the family to observe the examination. The court also summoned What should have been a straightforward process became a prolonged struggle The Njoku family’s Lawyer, Dr Christian C. Nwadigo, repeatedly raised concerns about Police conduct surrounding the implementation of the Coroner’s orders. RULAAC and the People’s Rights Organisation, subsequently petitioned the Police Service Commission alleging repeated failures to make Njoku’s body available for scheduled autopsies, including appointments on October 28 and October 30, 2025, notwithstanding repeated extensions granted by the court. Amnesty International subsequently reported that Tiger Base officials, failed on three occasions to appear for the court-ordered examination, even when court-appointed pathologists were present. This aspect of the case, deserves an investigation of its own. Lack of Accountability and Intimidation of Potential Witnesses When a person dies in State custody, preservation of the body, medical examination, documentation and independent investigation are not favours to the deceased’s family. They are indispensable safeguards against impunity. If officials implicated in a custodial death can delay or obstruct the very procedures designed to establish how that person died, the integrity of the entire accountability system is threatened. There was another disturbing development. During the inquest, concerns emerged that persons who had been detained alongside Njoku and who could potentially provide evidence about what happened inside Tiger Base, were themselves facing fresh Police attention.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/j.title_zh: 杰费斯·恩乔库：警察拘留期间死亡成为法治考验
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/j.body_zh: 杰斐斯·恩乔库被警方拘留时是活着的。他没有活着离开。他去世时32岁，此前在伊莫州警察指挥部反绑架组（俗称老虎基地，位于奥韦里）被拘留数周。对他的家人来说，悲剧并未随着他的死亡而结束。他们不得不开始另一场斗争：确定他如何死亡、确保进行尸检、保护潜在证人，并克服司法调查道路上反复设置的障碍。一年多后，奥韦里首席地方法官法庭作为验尸官法庭作出了值得全国关注的裁决。该裁决的重要性远远超出杰斐斯·恩乔库。它提出了根本性问题，即当公民在警察拘留设施的围墙后消失时会发生什么，以及家庭在试图让国家承担责任时面临的巨大困难。根据验尸官裁决的报告，恩乔库因涉嫌偷窃被拘留约六周——这通常是一项可保释的罪行。验尸官发现，有人要求支付金钱以换取他的释放，并驳回了随后将他描绘成恐怖分子以证明继续拘留合理的企图。据报道，法庭发现老虎基地的条件不符合被拘留者享有尊严、自由、法律代表和保释的权利，并指出了涉及酷刑、恐吓和勒索的做法。虽然医学证据据称将脑膜炎、支气管肺炎和高血压心脏病列为死亡原因之一，但验尸官作出了一个极其重要的裁决：恩乔库被拘留的条件和他被拘留的时长导致了他的健康恶化和最终死亡。这种区分很重要。一个人不必直接死于警察的子弹或警官的殴打，国家才对拘留期间的死亡承担责任。一旦国家剥夺一个人的自由，它就承担了保护该人生命、健康和身体完整的更高责任。警察拘留绝不能成为一个忽视疾病直到它致命的地方。或许，恩乔库案最令人不安的方面之一是他死后发生的事情。2025年6月11日，验尸官下令进行尸检，并规定由家属提名的独立病理学家观察检查。法庭还传唤了本应是一个直截了当的过程却变成了一场旷日持久的斗争。恩乔库家族的律师克里斯蒂安·C·恩瓦迪戈博士反复对警方在执行验尸官命令过程中的行为表示担忧。RULAAC和人民权利组织随后向警察服务委员会请愿，指控警方反复未能将恩乔库的尸体提供给预定的尸检，包括2025年10月28日和10月30日的预约，尽管法庭一再延长期限。大赦国际随后报告称，老虎基地官员在三次场合未能出席法庭下令的检查，即使法庭指定的病理学家在场。该案的这一方面值得单独调查。缺乏问责制和对潜在证人的恐吓当一个人在国家拘留期间死亡时，保存尸体、医学检查、记录和独立调查并不是对死者家属的恩惠。它们是防止有罪不罚的不可或缺的保障。如果与拘留死亡有关的官员能够延迟或阻挠旨在确定该人如何死亡的程序，那么整个问责制度的完整性就会受到威胁。还有另一个令人不安的事态发展。在调查期间，有人担心与恩乔库一起被拘留、可能提供老虎基地内部发生情况证据的人，自己正面临新的警方关注。

In a chat with THISDAY, Albanna said the core problem facing oil and gas is not lack of data, but fragmented data and knowledge that prevents operators and investors from seeing the true reality of an asset.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/e.summary_zh: 尼日利亚上游石油和天然气行业必须解决其数据整合挑战以释放储量并吸引融资，CypherCrescent创新总监纳迪亚·阿尔班纳博士表示。在与THISDAY的交谈中，阿尔班纳说石油和天然气面临的核心问题不是缺乏数据，而是碎片化的数据和知识，这阻碍了运营商和投资者看到资产的真实情况。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/e.body: The upstream oil and gas industry in Nigeria must solve its data integration challenge to unlock reserves and attract financing, Innovation Director at CypherCrescent, Dr Nadia Albanna, has said. In a chat with THISDAY, Albanna said the core problem facing oil and gas is not lack of data, but fragmented data and knowledge that prevents operators and investors from seeing the true reality of an asset. “The key for this problem that we have in oil and gas is integration,” she said. According to her, integration of data, integration of knowledge and translating that into the actual reality of the asset is central to improving asset performance and telling the story of an investable project. She noted that making a project bankable and financeable requires building investor confidence that they have the full picture, including risk elements and uncertainties around regulatory environment, subsurface realities, construction and development challenges. She described integrated technology solutions as critical to bridging the gap between technical understanding and financial decision-making. On the growing conversation around artificial intelligence in the energy sector, Albanna said AI is a powerful tool, but its effectiveness depends on data readiness and local expertise. She said a lot of data in Nigeria and other locations remain manual, fragmented and not collected in one place, requiring significant work in digitization and infrastructure for real-time data transfer and communication. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/p.title: Prof Agomoh Elected Global Torture Council President, Unveils Seven-Point Agenda
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/p.summary: Professor Uju Agomoh, a prominent Nigerian human rights advocate and Chairperson of the Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL), has unveiled a seven-point agenda after her election as President of the International Rehabilitation Council for Torture Victims (IRCT) for the 2026–2029 term.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/p.summary_zh: 著名尼日利亚人权倡导者、尼日利亚律师协会公共利益与发展法分会（NBA-SPIDEL）主席乌朱·阿戈莫教授在当选为酷刑受害者国际康复理事会（IRCT）2026-2029年任期主席后公布了一项七点议程。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/p.body: Professor Uju Agomoh, a prominent Nigerian human rights advocate and Chairperson of the Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL), has unveiled a seven-point agenda after her election as President of the International Rehabilitation Council for Torture Victims (IRCT) for the 2026–2029 term. Agomoh, who also heads Prisoners Rehabilitation and Welfare Action (PRAWA), was elected on October 16, 2026, to lead the international organisation dedicated to supporting torture survivors and advancing efforts to prevent torture worldwide. Her agenda focuses on strengthening member organisations, improving rehabilitation services, amplifying survivors’ voices and expanding the organisation’s global influence in the fight against torture. She pledged to begin with structured consultations across the organisation’s regions within her first three to six months in office, with a view to agreeing on priority outcomes with the Council. Dr Agomoh also pledged to promote the sustainability of member centres by leveraging donor relationships and partnerships, to create funding opportunities for organisations providing frontline services to survivors. Another key priority, is linking rehabilitation to torture prevention by drawing on the clinical expertise of member organisations to strengthen engagement with United Nations bodies, regional institutions and national preventive mechanisms. On survivors’ participation, she said their perspectives must influence governance, institutional priorities and programme design. She pledged to work with the IRCT’s Survivor Advisory Board, to ensure that people who have experienced torture have a meaningful voice in decisions affecting them. The new President also promised transparent governance, through regular reports to the Council on agreed objectives, including areas where progress falls short of expectations. To expand the organisation’s reach, Dr Agomoh plans to encourage the establishment of rehabilitation centres in countries and regions without IRCT member centres, while supporting locally led initiatives and sustaining existing members. She further pledged to strengthen advocacy through international, continental, regional and national mechanisms to promote torture prevention, rehabilitation and justice for survivors. The IRCT is a global network of rehabilitation organisations and independent experts providing medical, psychological, legal and social support to torture survivors. Its work also includes documenting torture, promoting accountability and advocating for survivors’ rights. Dr Agomoh’s presidency places a Nigerian human rights advocate at the head of an international network, working to improve the recovery and protection of torture survivors. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/p.title_zh: 阿戈莫教授当选全球酷刑理事会主席，公布七点议程
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/p.body_zh: 乌朱·阿戈莫教授是尼日利亚著名人权倡导者、尼日利亚律师协会公共利益与发展法分会（NBA-SPIDEL）主席，她在当选国际酷刑受害者康复理事会（IRCT）2026–2029年任期主席后，公布了一项七点议程。阿戈莫同时领导囚犯康复与福利行动组织（PRAWA），于2026年10月16日当选，领导这个致力于支持酷刑幸存者并在全球推进防止酷刑努力的国际组织。她的议程侧重于加强成员组织、改善康复服务、放大幸存者声音以及扩大该组织在反对酷刑斗争中的全球影响力。她承诺在上任后最初三至六个月内开始在该组织各区域进行结构化磋商，以期与理事会就优先成果达成一致。阿戈莫博士还承诺通过利用捐赠者关系和伙伴关系来促进成员中心的可持续性，为向幸存者提供一线服务的组织创造资金机会。另一个关键优先事项是将康复与酷刑预防联系起来，利用成员组织的临床专业知识来加强与联合国机构、区域机构和国家预防机制的互动。在幸存者参与方面，她表示他们的观点必须影响治理、机构优先事项和方案设计。她承诺与IRCT幸存者咨询委员会合作，确保经历过酷刑的人在影响他们的决定中拥有有意义的声音。新主席还承诺通过定期向理事会报告商定目标（包括进展未达到预期的情况）来实现透明治理。为了扩大该组织的覆盖范围，阿戈莫博士计划鼓励在没有IRCT成员中心的国家和地区建立康复中心，同时支持本地主导的举措并维持现有成员。她进一步承诺通过国际、大陆、区域和国家机制加强倡导，以促进酷刑预防、康复以及为幸存者伸张正义。IRCT是一个由康复组织和独立专家组成的全球网络，为酷刑幸存者提供医疗、心理、法律和社会支持。其工作还包括记录酷刑、促进问责并倡导幸存者权利。阿戈莫博士的主席职位将一位尼日利亚人权倡导者置于一个国际网络的领导位置，该网络致力于改善酷刑幸存者的康复和保护。THISDAY成立于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都特区及世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术对有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真理和理性，涵盖从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育、社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列问题。您可以通过hello@thisdaylive.com与我们联系，或访问我们的联系页面。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/k.title: Kidnap Trial: German-Based Nigerian Links Ex-Girlfriend to Abduction
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/k.summary: A Nigerian security officer based in Germany, Adekunle Adegboyega Aderinsoye, has told a Lagos High Court in Ikeja how his former girlfriend, Bunmi Mosaku, allegedly became linked to his kidnapping, following a brief relationship and a disputed pregnancy claim.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/k.summary_zh: 驻德国的尼日利亚安全官员阿德昆勒·阿德博耶加·阿德林索耶告诉伊凯贾拉各斯高等法院，他的前女友本米·莫萨库据称如何在一段短暂关系和有争议的怀孕声明之后与他被绑架一事产生关联。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/k.body: A Nigerian security officer based in Germany, Adekunle Adegboyega Aderinsoye, has told a Lagos High Court in Ikeja how his former girlfriend, Bunmi Mosaku, allegedly became linked to his kidnapping, following a brief relationship and a disputed pregnancy claim. Aderinsoye gave the account while testifying before Justice Hakeem Oshodi, in the trial of a chieftain of the National Union of Road Transport Workers, Ganiyu Oyedepo, popularly known as Koko Zaria, and Toheeb Adekunle, who are facing a six-count charge bordering on alleged kidnapping. Led in evidence by prosecution Counsel, Mrs O. Aluko, the witness said he returned to Germany after dating Mosaku for about two weeks in Nigeria. He said she subsequently contacted him, claiming to be pregnant, prompting him to send her money for the alleged pregnancy. According to him, his suspicions arose when he asked a friend to visit Mosaku unannounced and check on her, only for the friend to report that she was not pregnant. He said the discovery made him sever ties with her and her family. Aderinsoye further told the court that his suspicions deepened when he was allegedly abducted, and taken to a location where he saw Mosaku. He said his captors beat him, seized his laptop and wristwatch, and forced him to disclose the personal identification number of his First Bank ATM card before withdrawing money from his account. The witness alleged that he was subsequently taken to an uncompleted building, where his abductors demanded ₦5 million for his release. He said a friend eventually paid ₦500,000 to secure his freedom. The court admitted seven photographs, showing injuries allegedly sustained by the witness around his forehead and eyes as exhibits A1 to A7. During cross-examination, however, Aderinsoye acknowledged that he did not see the second Defendant at the hotel mentioned in the proceedings, or at the uncompleted building. He also told the court that he later returned to Germany, sought medical treatment, and made further statements to the Nigeria Police. Following the prosecution’s request for a subpoena to First Bank Plc, Justice Oshodi adjourned the case until February 9, 2027, for continuation of proceedings. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/k.title_zh: 绑架审判：在德国的尼日利亚人将前女友与绑架联系起来
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/k.body_zh: 一名驻德国的尼日利亚安全官员阿德昆勒·阿德博耶加·阿德林索耶向伊凯贾拉各斯高等法院讲述了他的前女友本米·莫萨库如何在短暂交往和有争议的怀孕声明之后据称与他被绑架一事有关。阿德林索耶在审判全国道路运输工人联盟酋长加尼尤·奥耶德波（俗称科科·扎里亚）和托希布·阿德昆勒时在法官哈基姆·奥肖迪面前作证，两人面临六项与据称绑架有关的指控。由检方律师O. 阿尔uko夫人引导作证时，该证人说他与莫萨库在尼日利亚约会约两周后返回德国。他说她随后联系他，声称自己怀孕，促使他寄钱给她用于所谓的怀孕。据他说，当他要求一位朋友突然拜访莫萨库并查看她的情况时，他的怀疑出现了，结果朋友报告说她没有怀孕。他说这一发现让他切断了与她及其家人的联系。阿德林索耶进一步告诉法院，当他据称被绑架并被带到一个他看到莫萨库的地方时，他的怀疑加深了。他说绑匪殴打他，没收了他的笔记本电脑和手表，并强迫他透露他的第一银行自动取款机卡的个人识别码，然后从他的账户中取款。该证人声称他随后被带到一栋未完工的建筑，他的绑架者要求支付500万奈拉以释放他。他说一位朋友最终支付了50万奈拉以确保他的自由。法院采纳了七张照片，作为A1至A7号证据，显示证人前额和眼睛周围据称遭受的伤口。然而，在交叉询问期间，阿德林索耶承认他没有在诉讼中提到的酒店或未完工的建筑中看到第二被告。他还告诉法院，他后来返回德国，寻求医疗治疗，并向尼日利亚警方作出进一步陈述。在检方要求向第一银行 Plc 发出传票后，奥肖迪法官将案件休庭至2027年2月9日以继续诉讼。THISDAY 成立于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都特区和世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术与有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真相和理性，涵盖从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列问题。您可以通过 hello@thisdaylive.com 给我们发邮件或访问我们的联系页面。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.summary: Nigerian Lawyer, Yusuf Temilola Nurudeen, has won the International Bar Association (IBA) Pro Bono Award, for his commitmentx to expanding access to justice for indigent and vulnerable people. Nurudeen received the award on October 8, 2026, during the IBA’s annual awards breakfast in Copenhagen, Denmark.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.summary_zh: 尼日利亚律师优素福·泰米洛拉·努鲁丁赢得了国际律师协会（IBA）公益奖，以表彰他致力于扩大贫困和弱势群体获得司法救济的机会。努鲁丁于2026年10月8日在丹麦哥本哈根举行的IBA年度颁奖早餐会上领取了该奖。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.body: Nigerian Lawyer, Yusuf Temilola Nurudeen, has won the International Bar Association (IBA) Pro Bono Award, for his commitmentx to expanding access to justice for indigent and vulnerable people. Nurudeen received the award on October 8, 2026, during the IBA’s annual awards breakfast in Copenhagen, Denmark. It was presented by Babatunde Ajibade, SAN, Chair of the IBA Section on Public and Professional Interest for 2025–2026. He dedicated the recognition to 141 volunteer Lawyers, working across 18 Nigerian States through the Foundation for Public Interest Law and Development, also known as The Pro Bono Centre, providing legal assistance to people unable to afford representation. In his acceptance speech, Nurudeen traced his commitment to justice to his upbringing in Ikotun, Lagos, where he became the first Lawyer in his family. He recalled how wrongful imprisonment could have deprived his father of freedom, and potentially ended his own professional ambitions. He highlighted vulnerable Nigerians who remain detained because they cannot afford Lawyers, women trapped in abusive marriages, children denied maintenance and families facing property losses without access to legal representation. Nurudeen insisted that poverty should never determine whether citizens can defend their rights, describing pro bono service as a professional responsibility, rather than charity. He said the award was not an indication that their work was finished, but an encouragement to expand their reach and deepen their commitment to justice. Nurudeen reaffirmed his determination to ensure that nobody is too poor to obtain legal defence, too powerless to be heard, or too marginalised to receive protection under the law. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.title_zh: 尼日利亚律师在哥本哈根赢得IBA公益奖
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/20/n.body_zh: 尼日利亚律师优素福·泰米洛拉·努鲁丁因致力于扩大贫困和弱势群体获得司法的机会，获得了国际律师协会（IBA）公益奖。努鲁丁于2026年10月8日在丹麦哥本哈根举行的国际律师协会年度颁奖早餐会上领取了该奖项。该奖项由2025–2026年度国际律师协会公共与职业利益部主席巴巴通德·阿吉巴德，SAN颁发。他将这一荣誉献给141名志愿律师，这些律师通过公共利益法律与发展基金会（也称为公益中心）在尼日利亚18个州开展工作，为无力负担代理费用的人提供法律援助。在获奖感言中，努鲁丁将自己对正义的承诺追溯到他在拉各斯伊科通的成长经历，他是家族中第一位律师。他回忆道，父亲曾可能因错误监禁而失去自由，并可能终结他自己的职业抱负。他强调了那些因无力负担律师费用而仍被拘留的脆弱尼日利亚人、陷入虐待婚姻的妇女、被剥夺抚养费的儿童以及无法获得法律代理而面临财产损失的家庭。努鲁丁坚持认为，贫困绝不应决定公民能否捍卫自己的权利，他将公益服务描述为一种职业责任，而非慈善。他说这个奖项并不表明他们的工作已经完成，而是鼓励他们扩大影响并深化对正义的承诺。努鲁丁重申了他的决心，即确保没有人因为太穷而无法获得法律辩护、太无力而无法被听到，或者太边缘化而无法获得法律保护。THISDAY成立于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都特区及世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术与有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真理和理性，涵盖从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育、社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列问题。您可以通过hello@thisdaylive.com与我们联系，或访问我们的联系页面

https://leadership.ng/dangote-accepts-ba.body: Nigerian content creator Adebayo Ridwan, popularly known as Bae U Barbie, has invited billionaire businessman Aliko Dangote to appear on his YouTube show, Curiosity Made Me Ask. Bae U made the invitation while asking Dangote about his media appearances, the need to engage younger Nigerians interested in his business, and the planned investment in his company. The content creator noted that many of Dangote’s interviews had been on platforms that younger audiences might not typically watch, despite their interest in investing in his business and participating in the company’s initial public offering. “Most of the interviews we’ve seen you have been on platforms that my generation don’t watch,” Bae U said. He added that young Nigerians were interested in investing in Dangote’s company and wanted to give him a platform to reach a wider audience. “I’m not saying you should sack your media team. No, but you know, when you finish,” he said before asking when the billionaire would appear on his show. Responding to the invitation, Dangote said young people represented the future and that older generations needed to share their experiences with them. “Honestly, the future that we have is actually you, the youth. We, our own generation, really, we have not really done very well for Nigeria and also for Africa. That’s the truth,” he said. Dangote said there was a need for conversations between older and younger generations to share experiences and discuss the country’s development. “So we need to sit down with some of you and discuss our own experience with you,” he added. The businessman noted that many young Nigerians had limited knowledge of some of the country’s past political leaders and historical experiences. He cited former President Olusegun Obasanjo as an example, saying younger Nigerians might know more about him because he returned to power. Bae U interjected, saying, “Thanks to me. I gave him the platform, sir,” apparently referring to his own interview with Obasanjo. Dangote agreed that younger audiences were an important group for him to engage. So really, you are right. Going forward, this sort of audience is the audience that we, somebody like me, should actually face,” he said. He added that young people had continued to show him support and respect, including when he travelled abroad. According to Dangote, people around him sometimes tried to prevent members of the public from taking photographs with him, but he preferred to oblige them. He recalled an experience from his youth when he and his grandfather met prominent figures in Washington and asked to have their photographs taken with them. Dangote said the experience influenced his willingness to take pictures with members of the public, despite his current status. “I wasn’t begging for anything. What I was saying, I was just saying that, God, you have over-blessed me,” he said. Dangote indicated that he was willing to sit down with younger people and share his experiences in an informal setting where they could ask questions about his journey. “We will come,” he said in response to the invitation to appear on Curiosity Made Me Ask. He added that he wanted the conversation to be open, allowing people to ask how he built his business and achieved his success. We’ve got the edge. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/promoted/.body: Governor Uba Sani has vowed that no community will be rendered homeless in Kaduna State because his administration believes in human dignity and the sanctity of life. The governor made the promise while distributing land titles to communities in Igabi local government, whose lands have been a subject of dispute between the military and the inhabitants. Comprising 704 houses, the benefitting communities include Unguwan Malam Auta, Unguwan Alhassan and Unguwan Lauya as well as Unguwan Aboki, Unguwan Danjuma, Unguwan Musa and Unguwan Yohana. The alleged land seizure took place before the coming of the present administration and when he came on board, Governor Uba Sani tried to resolve the matter amicably to no avail. Although the matter is still in court, he directed the Director General of Kaduna State Geographic Information Service(KADGIS), Dr Bashir Ibrahim Garba, to give plots of land to the affected communities, including farmlands. Speaking at the Birnin Yero Tsohuwa Primary School on Sunday, the Governor disclosed that there were over 5,000 people living within the affected communities and more than 2,000 of them had been displaced because of the land dispute. ‘’Today, we gathered here not only to give free plots of land to all the members of the communities and the households, we also here to ensure that we look at other problems. ‘’Apart from giving you plots of land, ensuring that all of you have decent shelter is important to our administration because we believe in the human dignity. We also gave each one of you a farmland as a means of livelihood because 90% of you are farmers,’’ he added. Governor Uba Sani also promised the communities five trucks of free fertiliser, in addition to extending a special intervention to enable them stand on their feet. ‘’I have directed the Secretary to Kaduna State Government, together with the Commissioner of Finance and Commissioner of Planning and Budget, to sit down with your leaders so as to support you with social intervention. ‘’We believe all the people here, particularly those that are vulnerable, deserve a level of compensation from our government. So, we are going to give you social intervention, so that some of you that have lost their livelihoods, will quickly go back to their activities, particularly those involved in small businesses,’’ he promised. Uba Sani commended the communities for living in peace irrespective of their ethno-religious differences and party affiliations. ‘’I’ve seen the level of togetherness between the Muslims and Christians within these communities. You work together as one family. When the incident happened, I was informed you treated each other as one family,’’ he added. In his welcome remarks, the Director General of KADGIS, Dr Bashir Ibrahim Garba, disclosed that the Governor Uba Sani administration has resolved 5,285 inherited land cases. ‘’The Governor has also supported more than 2,000 communities that were displaced by either disputes or land issues,’’ he added. Dr Garba commended the Governor for not only resolving the land matter but for also giving the communities farmlands that will sustain them because majority are farmers
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/promoted/.title_zh: 乌巴·萨尼解决10年土地纠纷，为704户提供地块、农田和免费肥料
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/promoted/.body_zh: 卡杜纳州州长乌巴·萨尼誓言，该州不会有任何社区因无家可归而流离失所，因为他的政府相信人的尊严和生命的神圣性。州长在向伊加比地方政府区的社区分发土地所有权证书时做出了这一承诺，这些社区的土地一直是军方与居民之间争端的主题。受益社区包括704栋房屋，具体有Unguwan Malam Auta、Unguwan Alhassan和Unguwan Lauya，以及Unguwan Aboki、Unguwan Danjuma、Unguwan Musa和Unguwan Yohana。所谓的土地没收事件发生在现政府上台之前，当他上任后，州长乌巴·萨尼试图友好解决此事，但未能成功。尽管此事仍在法院审理中，但他指示卡杜纳州地理信息服务局(KADGIS)局长巴希尔·易卜拉欣·加尔巴博士向受影响的社区提供土地地块，包括农田。周日在Birnin Yero Tsohuwa小学发表讲话时，州长透露，受影响社区内有超过5000人居住，其中超过2000人因土地争端而流离失所。“今天，我们聚集在这里，不仅要向社区所有成员和家庭免费提供土地地块，我们还在这里确保我们关注其他问题。”“除了给你们提供土地地块，确保你们所有人都有体面的住所对我们的政府很重要，因为我们相信人的尊严。我们还给你们每个人提供了一块农田作为生计手段，因为你们90%都是农民，”他补充说。州长乌巴·萨尼还承诺向这些社区提供五卡车免费化肥，并额外提供特别干预措施以帮助他们站稳脚跟。“我已指示卡杜纳州政府秘书长，连同财政专员和规划与预算专员，与你们的领导人坐下来，以便通过社会干预措施支持你们。”“我们相信这里的所有人，特别是那些脆弱群体，都值得从我们的政府获得一定程度的补偿。因此，我们将向你们提供社会干预措施，以便你们中一些失去生计的人能够迅速恢复他们的活动，特别是那些从事小生意的人，”他承诺。乌巴·萨尼赞扬这些社区无论民族宗教差异和党派归属如何，都和平相处。“我看到了这些社区内穆斯林和基督徒之间的团结程度。你们像一个家庭一样共同工作。当事件发生时，我被告知你们像一个家庭一样相互对待，”他补充说。在欢迎致辞中，KADGIS局长巴希尔·易卜拉欣·加尔巴博士透露，乌巴·萨尼州长政府已经解决了5285起继承的土地案件。“州长还支持了超过2000个因争端或土地问题而流离失所的社区，”他补充说。加尔巴博士赞扬州长不仅解决了土地问题，还为社区提供了能够维持他们生活的农田，因为大多数人是农民。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/hawa-koomson.body: The National Women’s Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Mavis Hawa Koomson, has called for a swift, independent and transparent investigation into allegations of sexual abuse involving 19 female students of Obuasi Senior High School (SHS). She has urged the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service to investigate the allegations and ensure that anyone found culpable faces the appropriate legal processes. The call follows an investigative report by Joy FM's Manasseh Azure Awuni, concerning allegations of rape, sexual harassment, sexual assault and other forms of abuse involving the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. In a statement issued on October 19, 2026, Hawa Koomson said the reports were particularly disturbing because some of the alleged incidents had reportedly been brought to the attention of school authorities as far back as March 2026, without meaningful action to protect the students. She stressed that the allegations must be investigated thoroughly and that accountability should not be influenced by political affiliation, social standing or the position of anyone implicated. “A child knows no political party colours. We must never subordinate the dignity, safety, and protection of our children to partisan considerations,” she said. The allegations have not been established, and the call for an investigation is intended to ensure that the facts are determined through due process. Hawa Koomson expressed concern over reports of possible intimidation, victimisation and reprisals against the students and their families. She called for measures to protect the identities of the affected students, guarantee their safety and preserve their dignity throughout any investigative and judicial proceedings. She also urged authorities to provide a safe and confidential environment for other potential victims to report similar experiences without fear of retaliation. The National Women’s Organiser called on the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection and the Ghana Education Service (GES) to work with child protection organisations and other relevant support groups to provide assistance to the students and their families. The support, she said, should include professional counselling, trauma-informed psychological care, medical attention and other protective measures. She further urged state institutions and civil society organisations to ensure that the welfare of the students remained central to every intervention. Beyond the immediate allegations, Hawa Koomson called on the GES to undertake a comprehensive review of child protection and safeguarding policies in schools. She said the situation raised questions about reporting procedures, supervision, professional conduct and accountability within educational institutions. She called for effective and enforceable systems to prevent sexual abuse and exploitation, respond promptly to complaints and protect students’ physical and psychological well-being. Hawa Koomson said the best interests of the child must remain paramount, in line with the Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560). “Our girls must feel safe, protected, respected and empowered within the very institutions established to nurture their potential and secure their future. No girl should ever be compelled to sacrifice her dignity, safety or fundamental rights in pursuit of education,” she said. She also appealed to women across the country, particularly the Vice-President, to take a keen and sustained interest in the matter and use their influence to support efforts to secure justice for the affected students. Hawa Koomson urged state institutions, traditional and religious leaders, child protection advocates and the general public to support a credible investigative process. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: The Rivers State House of Assembly has reversed its earlier decision declaring the seats of three lawmakers loyal to Governor Siminalayi Fubara vacant. The Assembly took the decision a day after FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, led lawmakers and the state’s 23 local government chairpersons to a reconciliation meeting with the governor in Port Harcourt. The lawmakers are Timothy Oruibienimigha, representing Opobo/Nkoro Constituency; Victor Jumbo , representing Bonny Constituency; and Sokari Goodboy Sokari, representing Ahoada West Constituency. Martins Wachukwu, a media aide to the speaker, announced the development in a statement posted on Facebook on Monday. According to the statement, the lawmakers apologised to the House for failing to resume legislative duties after their suspension was lifted in December 2023. They attributed their continued absence to their alleged failure to receive official correspondence informing them that the suspension had been lifted following a presidential intervention, the statement said. The lawmakers were among four members suspended on 30 October 2023 amid the political crisis that divided the assembly into factions loyal to Mr Wike and Mr Fubara. The statement said in Monday’s plenary, lawmakers debated the appeals and supported the request to rescind the earlier resolution declaring the seats vacant. Mr Amaewhule said, “Investigations indicated that the three lawmakers might not have received the correspondence notifying them of the lifting of their suspension,” the statement added. The lawmakers subsequently voted in favour of reversing the declaration, allowing their colleagues to return to the Assembly, according to the statement. The latest decision comes amid renewed efforts to reconcile Mr Wike and Mr Fubara after more than three years of political hostilities that have repeatedly disrupted governance in Rivers State. The political crisis in Rivers State began in 2023, months after Governor Fubara succeeded Mr Wike as governor. The disagreement between the former allies escalated into a struggle for control of the state’s political structures, including the House of Assembly. In October 2023, amid an impeachment attempt against Mr Fubara by lawmakers loyal to Mr Wike, the Assembly split into two factions. An overwhelming majority of 27 lawmakers backed Mr Wike, while four supported the governor. Edison Ehie, who led the four-member faction loyal to Mr Fubara, obtained a court order allowing the group to continue legislative proceedings and subsequently emerged as speaker of the factional Assembly. Mr Ehie resigned as speaker and as a member of the Assembly following a peace deal brokered by President Bola Tinubu in December 2023. Mr Fubara later appointed him chief of staff. In May 2024, Mr Jumbo emerged as speaker of the pro-Fubara faction after Mr Ehie’s departure. The faction continued to hold sittings and pass legislation, including considering budget proposals and screening commissioner nominees, while the Amaewhule-led faction also conducted legislative business. The legal battle over the Assembly’s leadership later shifted in favour of the Wike-backed lawmakers. In July 2024, the Court of Appeal reinstated the 27 lawmakers and recognised Martin Amaewhule as speaker. The Supreme Court subsequently ruled in February 2025 in favour of the Amaewhule-led Assembly, restoring the lawmakers’ status as legitimate members of the legislature. The ruling also affected the legal standing of decisions taken by the rival faction. In October 2024, the Amaewhule-led Assembly declared the seats of the three lawmakers now seeking reinstatement vacant, citing their continued absence from legislative sittings. The House said it had notified the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct elections to fill the vacancies.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.title_zh: 河流州议会恢复三名支持富巴拉的议员职务
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh: 里弗斯州议会已撤销此前宣布三位忠于州长 Siminalayi Fubara 的议员席位空缺的决定。议会在联邦首都区部长 Nyesom Wike 带领议员和该州 23 个地方政府主席与州长在哈科特港举行和解会议一天后作出这一决定。这些议员是代表 Opobo/Nkoro 选区的 Timothy Oruibienimigha、代表 Bonny 选区的 Victor Jumbo 以及代表 Ahoada West 选区的 Sokari Goodboy Sokari。议长媒体助理 Martins Wachukwu 周一在 Facebook 上发布的一份声明中宣布了这一进展。根据声明，这些议员就未能 在 2023 年 12 月 暂停被解除后恢复立法职责向议会道歉。他们将持续缺席归因于据称未收到通知他们因总统干预而解除暂停的正式函件，声明称。这些议员是 2023 年 10 月 30 日在将议会分裂为忠于 Wike 先生和 Fubara 先生派系的政治危机中被暂停的四名成员之一。声明称，在周一的全体会议上，议员们辩论了上诉并支持撤销先前宣布席位空缺的决议。Amaewhule 先生说，“调查表明，这三位议员可能没有收到通知他们解除暂停的函件，”声明补充说。这些议员随后投票赞成撤销该声明，允许他们的同事返回议会，根据声明。这一最新决定是在 Wike 先生和 Fubara 先生之间为期三年多的政治敌对之后重新努力和解的背景下作出的，这些敌对反复扰乱了里弗斯州的治理。里弗斯州的政治危机始于 2023 年，即 Fubara 州长接替 Wike 先生担任州长几个月后。前盟友之间的分歧升级为争夺该州政治结构控制权的斗争，包括议会。2023 年 10 月，在忠于 Wike 先生的议员试图弹劾 Fubara 先生期间，议会分裂为两个派系。27 名议员的压倒性多数支持 Wike 先生，而四名支持州长。领导忠于 Fubara 先生的四人派系的 Edison Ehie 获得法院命令，允许该团体继续立法程序，随后成为派系议会的议长。Ehie 先生在 2023 年 12 月由总统 Bola Tinubu 促成的和平协议后辞去议长和议会议员职务。Fubara 先生后来任命他为幕僚长。2024 年 5 月，在 Ehie 先生离开后，Jumbo 先生成为亲 Fubara 派系的议长。该派系继续举行会议并通过立法，包括审议预算提案和筛选专员提名人，而 Amaewhule 领导的派系也开展立法工作。关于议会领导权的法律斗争后来转向有利于 Wike 支持的议员。2024 年 7 月，上诉法院恢复了 27 名议员的职位并承认 Martin Amaewhule 为议长。最高法院随后于 2025 年 2 月作出有利于 Amaewhule 领导的议会的裁决，恢复了议员作为立法机关合法成员的地位。该裁决还影响了对手派系所作决定的法律地位。2024 年 10 月，Amaewhule 领导的议会宣布现在寻求恢复职位的三位议员席位空缺，理由是他们持续缺席立法会议。议会表示已通知独立国家选举委员会（INEC）举行选举以填补空缺。

https://punchng.com/tinubu-extends-tenur.body: President Bola Tinubu has approved an 18-month extension of the tenures of the Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Sylvester Ndidi Nwakuche, and the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nanna Nandap. The extension means Nwakuche will remain in office until May 26, 2028, while Nandap’s tenure will end on June 30, 2028. The approval was disclosed in a statement issued on Monday by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. According to the statement, the extension followed a recommendation by the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, to address a succession gap in both services and allow their boards sufficient time to appoint successors. “President Tinubu commended Nwakuche and Nandap for the reforms achieved under their leadership and charged them to consolidate these gains,” the statement said. Onanuga said Nwakuche was nominated by Tinubu as Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service in December 2024, and his appointment was confirmed by the Senate in March 2025. Nandap was nominated as Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service on February 21, 2024, and confirmed by the Senate on March 1, 2024. https://www.myjoyonline.com/government-m.body: The government has mobilised approximately GH¢436 million for the payment of Book and Research Allowances to eligible tertiary institutions across the country, according to Hashmin Mohammed, spokesperson for the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu. In a Facebook post on Monday, October 19, 2026, Mr Mohammed said GH¢238 million had already been disbursed to 56 institutions under the first batch of payments, while approximately GH¢198 million had been earmarked for the second batch. The University of Ghana is among the institutions expected to benefit from the subsequent disbursement. Mr Mohammed attributed the delay in payment to the University of Ghana to the late submission of required documentation to the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) for validation. He explained that the documents must be verified before the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) can process the payment. The spokesperson said the validation and documentation requirements form part of the administrative procedures intended to ensure that public funds are accurately processed and disbursed to the appropriate institutions. He did not indicate when the University of Ghana’s payment would be completed. The Book and Research Allowance is paid to eligible lecturers in public tertiary institutions to support their academic and research work. Delays in the payment of the allowance have periodically attracted concern from beneficiaries, making the government’s disbursement arrangements an issue of interest to tertiary education staff. With the first batch reportedly paid and the second batch earmarked for disbursement, attention will be on the completion of the outstanding administrative processes and the release of funds to the remaining eligible institutions

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: Former Minister of Power and Steel, Liyel Imoke, said Monday that the controversial Mambilla Hydropower station contract was awarded by his predecessor Olu Agunloye with the approval of the Federal Executive Council (FEC). Mr Imoke said it was unnecessary to formally cancel the contract after he assumed office, because the contract never received the blessing of the FEC in the first place. The former Cross River State governor was fielding questions at the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, where he appeared as the sixth prosecution witness in Mr Agunloye’s corruption trial. Mr Imoke succeeded Mr Agunloye as the power minister in July 2003 and served until January 2007, during former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration. Mr Imoke later became the Governor of Cross River State in May 2007 and served in that capacity until May 2015. The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) called Mr Imoke as its sixth prosecution witness against Mr Agunloye, who faces seven charges including disobedience to a presidential directive, conspiracy, forgery and receiving gratification. The charges stemmed from his roles in the award of the $6 billion Mambilla Hydroelectric Power contract in May 2003 to Sunrise Power and Transmission Company Limited (SPTCL). An arbitration panel in Paris, France, recently cleared Nigeria of any liability regarding the contract while it accused PTCL of fraud in its ….. The project was a proposed 3,050 MW hydroelectric facility located in Kakara village, Taraba State, which never saw the light of the day. The prosecution said Mr Agunloye disobeyed a presidential directive issued in 2003 during a Federal Executive Council meeting regarding the contract. The EFCC also accused Mr Agunloye of conspiring with Leno Adesanya, the major prompter of SPTCL who the agency indicated was at large, to falsify a document titled “Construction of 3,960MW Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Station on a Build, Operate and Transfer Basis” in 2003. Other allegations include receiving gratifications of over N5 million from SPTCL and Mr Adesanya. An arbitration tribunal recently exonerated Nigeria regarding the contract after finding that the award of the contract to SPTCL was tainted by bribery. Trial Judge Jude Onwuegbuzie listened on Monday as Mr Imoke, under cross-examination by Mr Agunloye’s defence lawyer Adeola Adedipe, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), maintained that the Mambilla power station contract was null and void in the first place, and required no formal pronouncement for its cancellation. “A contract awarded in contravention of the FEC will not require cancellation,” the politician said. “I did not cancel the contract because the FEC did not approve it, and so it was null and void. The minister does not have the power to award a contract. Similarly, the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power project became a subject of international concern. The project, first awarded in 2003 to SPTCL by the President Olusegun Obasanjo administration, is the subject of decades of a legal dispute. An arbitration tribunal in Paris recently resolved the matter in favour of Nigeria and against SPTCL, which had accused Nigeria of breach of contract. Mr Obasanjo, in 2023, accused Mr Agunloye of fraudulently awarding the contract to the company without approval. However, the former minister dismissed these claims, alleging that he was being used as a scapegoat to escape sanctions by the arbitration panel in Paris for abandoning contractual agreements on the project. The project, intended to generate 3,960 megawatts of electricity, was designed to be executed on a build, operate, and transfer basis. On Monday, Mr Imoke went down the memory lane about the controversial contract. Mr Imoke, who took office as the power minister in July 2003, recalled writing a letter dated 3 September 2003 in response to SPCL’s payment inquiry about the Mambilla power contract.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 60亿美元曼比拉电力合同：前州长利耶尔·伊莫克出庭作证指控前电力部长阿贡洛耶
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 前电力和钢铁部长利耶尔·伊莫克周一表示，有争议的曼比拉水电站合同是由他的前任奥卢·阿贡洛耶在联邦执行委员会（FEC）批准下授予的。伊莫克先生说，他上任后没有必要正式取消该合同，因为该合同从一开始就没有得到联邦执行委员会的批准。这位前克罗斯河州州长在联邦首都区（FCT）阿布贾接受提问时表示，他作为第六名检方证人出现在阿贡洛耶先生的腐败审判中。伊莫克先生于2003年7月接替阿贡洛耶先生担任电力部长，一直任职至2007年1月，当时正值前总统奥卢塞贡·奥巴桑乔执政期间。伊莫克先生后来于2007年5月成为克罗斯河州州长，并担任该职务直至2015年5月。经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）传唤伊莫克先生作为针对阿贡洛耶先生的第六名检方证人，阿贡洛耶面临七项指控，包括违抗总统指令、共谋、伪造文件和收受好处。这些指控源于他在2003年5月将价值60亿美元的曼比拉水电站合同授予日出电力和输电有限公司（SPTCL）中所扮演的角色。法国巴黎的一个仲裁小组最近清除了尼日利亚与该合同相关的任何责任，同时指控PTCL存在欺诈行为……该项目是一个拟建的3050兆瓦水电站，位于塔拉巴州的卡卡拉村，但从未实现。检方表示，阿贡洛耶先生违抗了2003年在联邦执行委员会会议上就该合同发布的总统指令。EFCC还指控阿贡洛耶先生与SPTCL的主要推动者莱诺·阿德萨尼亚共谋，后者被该机构指出目前在逃，于2003年伪造了一份题为“以建设、运营和转让方式建设3960兆瓦曼比拉水电站”的文件。其他指控包括从SPTCL和阿德萨尼亚先生那里收受超过500万奈拉的好处。一个仲裁法庭最近在发现将合同授予SPTCL的行为受到贿赂玷污后，就该合同免除了尼日利亚的责任。审判法官朱德·翁韦格布齐周一听取了伊莫克先生的证词，在阿贡洛耶先生的辩护律师、尼日利亚高级律师（SAN）阿德奥拉·阿德迪佩的交叉询问下，伊莫克坚持认为曼比拉电站合同从一开始就是无效的，不需要正式宣布取消。“一项违反联邦执行委员会规定的合同不需要取消，”这位政治家说。“我没有取消该合同，因为联邦执行委员会没有批准它，因此它是无效的。部长没有权力授予合同。同样，曼比拉水电站项目成为国际关注的对象。该项目于2003年首次由奥卢塞贡·奥巴桑乔政府授予SPTCL，是数十年法律纠纷的主题。巴黎的一个仲裁法庭最近解决了此事，有利于尼日利亚，不利于SPTCL，后者曾指控尼日利亚违约。奥巴桑乔先生在2023年指控阿贡洛耶先生欺诈性地在未经批准的情况下将合同授予该公司。然而，这位前部长驳斥了这些说法，声称他被当作替罪羊，以逃避巴黎仲裁小组因放弃项目合同协议而实施的制裁。该项目旨在发电3960兆瓦，设计以建设、运营和转让方式执行。周一，伊莫克先生回顾了这份有争议的合同。伊莫克先生于2003年7月就任电力部长，他回忆起写了一封日期为2003年9月3日的信，以回应SPCL关于曼比拉电力合同的付款询问。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/n.summary_zh: 联邦政府在埃塞俄比亚亚的斯亚贝巴的一个大陆论坛上展示了其Renewed Hope住房公私伙伴关系（PPP）模式，吸引了希望在住房项目中复制这一举措的非洲国家的兴趣。在谈到尼日利亚的住房倡议时，Ewalefoh解释说，Renewed Hope Cities项目将通过涉及私营部门的合资特许经营，在全国选定城市交付100,000套住房单位。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/n.body: The Federal Government has showcased its Renewed Hope Housing Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model at a continental forum in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, attracting interest from African countries seeking to replicate the initiative in their housing programmes. The presentation was made by the Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh, at the Second Forum for Public-Private Partnership Units in Africa, held at Africa Hall, United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), with delegations from 36 countries in attendance. According to a press release issued by Ifeanyi Nwoko, ICRC Acting Head, Media and Publicity, on Monday, the forum was co-organised by the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, the African Development Bank (AfDB) and the African Legal Support Facility under the theme, “Making Social Sector PPPs Work: From Policy Ambition to Effective Service Delivery”. The forum focused on how public-private partnerships could support the delivery of affordable housing, healthcare, education, sanitation and water services across the continent. Nigeria was among five countries that presented projects at the forum’s project clinic, alongside Malawi, Kenya, Djibouti and Côte d’Ivoire. Speaking on Nigeria’s housing initiative, Ewalefoh explained that the Renewed Hope Cities programme would deliver 100,000 housing units across selected cities in the country through a joint venture concession involving the private sector. “The beauty of this PPP structure is that it is not the conventional PPP. In this case, the private party owns the land, has the design, is financing it and is doing the construction,” he said. He explained that under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, the government’s responsibility was to reduce the risks that could discourage private investment in housing. “The PPP here is that government agreed to de-risk the project,” Ewalefoh said. The ICRC director-general noted that commercial lending rates in Nigeria, which exceed 23 per cent, had made housing finance expensive for developers and prospective homeowners. To address the challenge, the government introduced measures to reduce investment risks and improve affordability. These include designating middle-income federal civil servants as off-takers, committing to the construction of access roads to semi-urban project sites, and providing access to concessionary financing. The Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria unlocked about $19 million in single-digit interest funding, while the Family Homes Fund provided a further $20 million in concessionary loans. Additionally, buyers benefit from lower mortgage rates through an approximately $112 million MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund. The government also negotiated sale prices with the developer to keep the houses affordable and imposed a limit of one housing unit per buyer to discourage speculation. According to the statement, the measures reduced the effective cost of the project by about 30 per cent. The financing arrangement enables the government to facilitate housing delivery without directly financing the construction costs. About $39 million in concessionary funding is helping to unlock a project with construction costs of approximately $125 million in private-sector investment. “Government does not need to finance housing capital projects. It can crowd in private capital through policy, land availability and off-taker facilitation to create a replicable, scalable model for housing delivery,” Ewalefoh told delegates. The model generated considerable interest during the question-and-answer session, with delegates seeking to understand how Nigeria’s risk-reduction mechanisms, particularly the off-taker guarantee and access to concessionary finance, could be adapted to their respective countries.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/n.title_zh: 尼日利亚在大陆论坛展示更新希望住房公私合作模式，吸引非洲国家复制兴趣
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/n.body_zh: 联邦政府在埃塞俄比亚亚的斯亚贝巴举行的非洲大陆论坛上展示了其复兴希望住房公私合作（PPP）模式，吸引了希望在住房项目中复制该举措的非洲国家的兴趣。基础设施特许经营监管委员会（ICRC）总干事乔布森·奥塞奥迪翁·埃瓦莱福博士在非洲联合国经济委员会（UNECA）非洲大厅举行的非洲公私合作单位第二次论坛上进行了介绍，有来自36个国家的代表团出席。根据ICRC代理媒体与宣传主管伊费安伊·恩沃科周一发布的新闻稿，该论坛由联合国非洲经济委员会、非洲开发银行（AfDB）和非洲法律支持基金共同组织，主题为“让社会部门公私合作发挥作用：从政策雄心到有效服务交付”。论坛重点讨论了公私合作如何支持在整个非洲大陆提供负担得起的住房、医疗保健、教育、卫生和供水服务。尼日利亚是五个在论坛项目诊所展示项目的国家之一，另外还有马拉维、肯尼亚、吉布提和科特迪瓦。在谈到尼日利亚的住房举措时，埃瓦莱福解释说，复兴希望城市计划将通过涉及私营部门的合资特许经营，在该国选定城市交付10万套住房单元。“这种PPP结构的优点在于它不是传统的PPP。在这种情况下，私人一方拥有土地、拥有设计、正在为其提供资金并且正在进行建设，”他说。他解释说，在博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统的复兴希望议程下，政府的责任是降低可能阻碍住房领域私人投资的风险。“这里的PPP是政府同意为项目去风险，”埃瓦莱福说。ICRC总干事指出，尼日利亚的商业贷款利率超过23%，这使得住房融资对开发商和潜在房主来说变得昂贵。为了应对这一挑战，政府采取了措施来降低投资风险并提高可负担性。这些措施包括指定中等收入联邦公务员作为承购方，承诺为半城市项目地点建设通路道路，并提供优惠融资渠道。尼日利亚联邦抵押银行解锁了约1900万美元的个位数利率资金，而家庭住房基金提供了另外2000万美元的优惠贷款。此外，买家通过约1.12亿美元的MOFI房地产投资基金获得较低的抵押贷款利率。政府还与开发商谈判销售价格以保持房屋可负担，并对每位买家限制一套住房单元以阻止投机。根据声明，这些措施将项目的有效成本降低了约30%。融资安排使政府能够在不直接资助建设成本的情况下促进住房交付。约3900万美元的优惠资金正在帮助解锁一个建设成本约为1.25亿美元的私营部门投资项目。“政府不需要为住房资本项目提供资金。它可以通过政策、土地可用性和承购方便利来吸引私人资本，从而创造一个可复制、可扩展的住房交付模式，”埃瓦莱福告诉代表们。该模式在问答环节产生了相当大的兴趣，代表们寻求了解如何将尼日利亚的风险降低机制，特别是承购方担保和优惠融资渠道，适应到他们各自的国家。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/japan-motors.body: The Ministry of Food and Agriculture has announced that Japan Motors Trading Company Limited has donated five branded motorcycles towards the 42nd National Farmers’ Day celebration. In a press release issued on Monday, October 19, 2026, the Ministry said the donation qualified the company as a silver sponsor of the annual event, which recognises the contributions of farmers and fishers to Ghana’s development. “The Ministry remains deeply grateful to the Company for its dedicated commitment to support the celebration and the promotion of agricultural development in Ghana,” the statement, signed by the Ministry’s Public Relations Unit, said. The Ministry described the donation as a recognition of the important role farmers and fishers play in national development and an example of private-sector support for agricultural promotion. It called on other corporate organisations, financial institutions, development partners and individuals to contribute towards the upcoming celebration. The Ministry said the annual event provides a national platform to recognise the hard work and achievements of farmers and fishers, whose activities are central to food security, employment and economic growth. National Farmers’ Day is an annual celebration held to honour farmers and fishers across Ghana for their contributions to agricultural production and national food security. The 42nd edition is expected to take place later this year, with corporate sponsors and other partners supporting its organisation. Japan Motors’ donation adds to the support being mobilised for the celebration as the Ministry encourages more private-sector participation
