https://leadership.ng/dangote-refinery-e.title: Dangote Refinery Eyes Engaging More Indigenous Engineers, Services Firms
https://leadership.ng/dangote-refinery-e.summary: To achieve this the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals is engaging the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), for stronger local capacity to maintain and operate refineries, as industry stakeholders seek to reduce dependence on imported technology and services.
https://leadership.ng/dangote-refinery-e.summary_zh: 为实现这一目标，丹戈特石油炼油厂和石化公司正在与尼日利亚本地内容开发与监督委员会（NCDMB）合作，以加强本地能力来维护和运营炼油厂，因为行业利益相关者寻求减少对进口技术和服务的依赖。
https://leadership.ng/dangote-refinery-e.body: To achieve this the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals is engaging the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), for stronger local capacity to maintain and operate refineries, as industry stakeholders seek to reduce dependence on imported technology and services. Both parties urged a decisive transition from mere regulatory compliance to a stronger national commitment anchored on technological innovation and sustainable financing. They emphasized that these pillars are critical to deepening Nigerian content and driving accelerated industrial growth. The retreat convened key stakeholders from the oil and gas sector alongside representatives of relevant government institutions, fostering collaboration to tackle operational challenges and broaden indigenous participation across Nigeria’s energy value chain. At the heart of the discussions was a shared imperative: to ensure that Nigerian content transcends statutory obligations and becomes a sustainable national economic strategy that creates jobs, develops technical expertise, strengthens local supply chains and retains greater value within the country. In his keynote address, the Executive Secretary of NCDMB, Engr. Felix Omatsola Ogbe, represented by the Senior Technical Adviser and Director of the Project Certification and Authorisation Director (PCAD), Engr. Austin Uzoka, identified commitment, technology and financing as three fundamental requirements for building a resilient Nigerian content ecosystem. He challenged stakeholders to look beyond compliance and confront the deeper questions of industrial sustainability, particularly how Nigeria could maintain its major industrial assets, strengthen domestic supply chains and ensure that investments in critical infrastructure deliver lasting economic value. Drawing attention to the challenges associated with the country’s publicly owned refineries, Ogbe, emphasised the need to safeguard the sustainability of the Dangote Refinery by developing the goods, works, services and supply-chain capabilities required to support its continuous operations. The central message was clear: constructing world-class industrial facilities is only part of the task; building and maintaining the indigenous capabilities that sustain them is equally important. He stressed the need for credible supply chains capable of supporting industrial facilities, developing local capabilities and ensuring that such expertise remains resident in Nigeria. Without reliable domestic supply chains, he warned, the economic benefits of industrial investments could continue to flow outside the country, limiting local value creation and value addition. On technology, the Executive Secretary underscored the importance of developing Nigerian expertise to operate, maintain and sustain industrial facilities, rather than relying indefinitely on external capabilities. He also highlighted access to financing as a major constraint facing indigenous businesses. High interest rates and delays in accessing funds, he noted, can prevent Nigerian enterprises from executing projects, expanding operations and competing effectively within the oil and gas value chain. Ogbe further challenged stakeholders to consider how Nigeria could nurture the next generation of large-scale indigenous industrialists and support other Nigerian investors seeking to establish refineries and related facilities. Acknowledging Dangote Group’s pioneering contribution to industrial development, he urged the industry to help emerging indigenous investors succeed, noting that a stronger domestic refining sector would position Nigeria as a major oil and gas hub. Beyond its regulatory responsibilities, NCDMB used the retreat to reiterate its commitment to creating an enabling environment in which Nigerian businesses can participate meaningfully, build technical competence and compete for opportunities across the oil and gas industry.
https://leadership.ng/dangote-refinery-e.title_zh: 丹戈特炼油厂着眼于聘用更多本土工程师和服务公司
https://leadership.ng/dangote-refinery-e.body_zh: 为实现这一目标，丹戈特石油炼油厂和石化公司正在与尼日利亚本地内容开发与监督委员会（NCDMB）合作，以加强本地能力来维护和运营炼油厂，因为行业利益相关者寻求减少对进口技术和服务的依赖。双方敦促果断转变，从单纯的监管合规转向以技术创新和可持续融资为基础的更强有力的国家承诺。他们强调，这些支柱对于深化尼日利亚本地内容和推动加速的工业增长至关重要。此次务虚会召集了石油和天然气行业的关键利益相关者以及相关政府机构的代表，促进合作以解决运营挑战并扩大尼日利亚能源价值链中的本土参与。讨论的核心是一个共同的当务之急：确保尼日利亚本地内容超越法定义务，成为一项可持续的国家经济战略，该战略创造就业、发展技术专长、加强本地供应链并在国内保留更大价值。在其主旨演讲中，NCDMB执行秘书Engr. Felix Omatsola Ogbe（由高级技术顾问兼项目认证和授权局（PCAD）局长Engr. Austin Uzoka代表）将承诺、技术和融资确定为构建 resilient 尼日利亚本地内容生态系统的三个基本要求。他挑战利益相关者超越合规，并面对工业可持续性的更深层问题，特别是尼日利亚如何维护其主要工业资产、加强国内供应链并确保对关键基础设施的投资带来持久的经济价值。Ogbe提请注意与该国公有炼油厂相关的挑战，强调需要通过开发支持其持续运营所需的货物、工程、服务和供应链能力来保障丹戈特炼油厂的可持续性。核心信息很明确：建设世界级的工业设施只是任务的一部分；建设和维护维持这些设施的本土能力同样重要。他强调需要可靠的供应链来支持工业设施、发展本地能力并确保此类专长留在尼日利亚。他警告说，如果没有可靠的国内供应链，工业投资的经济效益可能会继续流向国外，限制本地价值创造和增值。在技术方面，执行秘书强调发展尼日利亚专长来运营、维护和维持工业设施的重要性，而不是无限期依赖外部能力。他还强调获得融资是本土企业面临的主要制约因素。他指出，高利率和获取资金的延误可能会阻止尼日利亚企业执行项目、扩大运营并在石油和天然气价值链中有效竞争。Ogbe进一步挑战利益相关者考虑尼日利亚如何培育下一代大型本土实业家并支持其他寻求建立炼油厂和相关设施的尼日利亚投资者。在承认丹戈特集团对工业发展的开创性贡献时，他敦促行业帮助新兴本土投资者取得成功，并指出更强大的国内炼油部门将使尼日利亚成为主要的石油和天然气枢纽。除了其监管职责之外，NCDMB利用此次务虚会重申其致力于创造一个使尼日利亚企业能够有意义地参与、建立技术能力并在石油和天然气行业中竞争机会的有利环境。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.summary: The Institute for Dietetics in Nigeria (IDN) has urged the National Assembly to withdraw consideration of a proposed bill seeking to establish the Nutritionists Registration Council of Nigeria, warning that it could promote quackery and weaken professional standards.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.summary_zh: 尼日利亚饮食学会敦促国民议会撤回对一项拟议法案的审议，该法案旨在建立尼日利亚营养师注册委员会，并警告称这可能助长庸医行为并削弱专业标准。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body: The Institute for Dietetics in Nigeria (IDN) has urged the National Assembly to withdraw consideration of a proposed bill seeking to establish the Nutritionists Registration Council of Nigeria, warning that it could promote quackery and weaken professional standards. The institute said the bill, if passed, could create confusion among regulatory bodies and undermine efforts to ensure that only qualified professionals practise in the nutrition and dietetics field. The institute’s National President, Tajudeen Ahmed, gave the warning while speaking with journalists at the National Assembly on Monday. Mr Ahmed argued that the priority should be to complete the legislative process for the Dietitians Council of Nigeria (Establishment) Bill, introduced in the House of Representatives in 2022, rather than pursue another bill that could create overlapping regulatory responsibilities. The House of Representatives passed the Dietitians Council of Nigeria Bill (HB 515) in May 2023 to provide a statutory framework for regulating the dietetics profession. The Senate subsequently passed the bill in October 2025. The bill awaits presidential assent, while a separate bill to establish the Nutritionists Registration Council of Nigeria has since emerged in the House of Representatives. Mr Ahmed said the proposed legislation for the Nutritionists Registration Council did not adequately ensure that only qualified and certified professionals were permitted to practise in the nutrition and dietetics field. “IDN supports the proper statutory regulation of qualified professionals working in nutrition and dietetics. However, HB 2659, reportedly promoted with the support of the Nutrition Society of Nigeria (NSN), is not the appropriate framework for achieving that objective. In its present form, the Bill threatens to create a parallel regulatory body with powers that substantially overlap with those already provided under the Dietitians Council of Nigeria (Establishment) Bill, 2022 (HB 515). “The establishment of two regulatory councils exercising competing authority over nutrition and dietetics education, accreditation, registration, clinical practice and professional discipline would create confusion, institutional conflict and avoidable expenditure. It would also weaken, rather than strengthen, the protection available to patients and the Nigerian public,” he said. Mr Ahmed said the Dietitians Council of Nigeria bill already provided a comprehensive framework for regulating the nutrition and dietetics profession. He argued that establishing the proposed Nutritionists Registration Council would duplicate provisions already covered by the earlier bill. “The Dietitians Council of Nigeria Bill already provides an extensive framework for regulating nutrition and dietetics. Its provisions cover professional education, registration, ethical standards, public-health nutrition, community practice, research, policy collaboration, food systems, public education and clinical dietetic practice. “Consequently, the proposed Nutritionists Registration Council would reproduce many of the same responsibilities and create uncertainty over which council should regulate integrated Nutrition and Dietetics programmes offered by Nigerian universities, polytechnics and colleges of health sciences and technology,” he said. Dietitians and nutritionists play important roles in preventing and managing diseases, improving maternal and child health, and addressing malnutrition, which remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria. Their work extends beyond advising people on what to eat. In hospitals, dietitians assess patients’ nutritional needs and develop appropriate dietary plans to support treatment and recovery. They help manage nutrition-related complications among patients with diabetes, kidney disease, cardiovascular conditions and other illnesses, as well as those recovering from surgery or living with severe malnutrition.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.title_zh: 尼日利亚营养师敦促NASS撤回营养师理事会法案，警告会出现庸医
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body_zh: 尼日利亚饮食学研究所（IDN）敦促国民议会撤回对一项拟议法案的审议，该法案旨在设立尼日利亚营养师注册委员会，并警告称这可能助长庸医行为并削弱专业标准。该研究所表示，如果该法案获得通过，可能会在监管机构之间造成混乱，并破坏确保只有合格专业人员才能在营养和饮食学领域执业的努力。该研究所全国主席塔朱丁·艾哈迈德周一在国民议会与记者交谈时发出了这一警告。艾哈迈德先生认为，优先事项应该是完成2022年在众议院提出的尼日利亚营养师委员会（设立）法案的立法程序，而不是追求另一项可能造成监管职责重叠的法案。众议院于2023年5月通过了尼日利亚营养师委员会法案（HB 515），以提供监管饮食学专业的法定框架。参议院随后于2025年10月通过了该法案。该法案等待总统批准，而另一项设立尼日利亚营养师注册委员会的单独法案此后已在众议院出现。艾哈迈德先生表示，为营养师注册委员会提出的立法没有充分确保只有合格且有证书的专业人员才被允许在营养和饮食学领域执业。“IDN支持对从事营养和饮食学的合格专业人员进行适当的法定监管。然而，据称在尼日利亚营养学会（NSN）支持下提出的HB 2659，并不是实现这一目标的适当框架。以其目前的形式，该法案威胁要创建一个平行监管机构，其权力与2022年尼日利亚营养师委员会（设立）法案（HB 515）已规定的权力存在大量重叠。”“设立两个监管委员会，对营养和饮食学教育、认证、注册、临床实践和专业纪律行使相互竞争的权力，将造成混乱、机构冲突和不必要的开支。它还将削弱而不是加强为患者和尼日利亚公众提供的保护，”他说。艾哈迈德先生表示，尼日利亚营养师委员会法案已经为监管营养和饮食学专业提供了一个全面的框架。他认为，设立拟议的营养师注册委员会将重复先前法案已涵盖的规定。“尼日利亚营养师委员会法案已经为监管营养和饮食学提供了一个广泛的框架。其条款涵盖专业教育、注册、道德标准、公共卫生营养、社区实践、研究、政策合作、食品系统、公众教育和临床饮食学实践。”“因此，拟议的营养师注册委员会将复制许多相同的职责，并造成不确定性，即哪个委员会应该监管尼日利亚大学、理工学院以及健康科学和技术学院提供的综合营养和饮食学课程，”他说。营养师和营养学家在预防和管理疾病、改善母婴健康以及解决营养不良方面发挥着重要作用，营养不良仍是尼日利亚主要的公共卫生挑战。他们的工作超出了就吃什么向人们提供建议。在医院中，营养师评估患者的营养需求并制定适当的饮食计划以支持治疗和康复。他们帮助管理糖尿病、肾脏疾病、心血管疾病和其他疾病患者以及从手术中恢复或患有严重营养不良的患者的营养相关并发症。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/r.summary_zh: 该协会支持对合格营养和饮食专业人员进行法定监管，它表示拟议的立法，即被确定为HB 2659的法案，将与尼日利亚营养师委员会（设立）法案2022（指定为HB 515）存在大量重叠。该协会的干预发生在关于营养和饮食专业人员适当监管结构的立法辩论期间，拟议的HB 2659寻求为营养师建立一个单独的委员会。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/r.body: Says proposed council could duplicate existing regulatory powers The Institute for Dietetics in Nigeria (IDN) has urged the National Assembly to reject a proposed bill seeking to establish the Nutritionists Registration Council of Nigeria, warning that its passage could create competing regulatory authorities, weaken professional standards and expose Nigerians to inadequately trained practitioners. The institute, which supports statutory regulation of qualified nutrition and dietetics professionals, said the proposed legislation, identified as HB 2659, would substantially overlap with the Dietitians Council of Nigeria (Establishment) Bill, 2022, designated HB 515. It called on the House of Representatives to discontinue consideration of HB 2659 in its present form and urged the Federal Government and National Assembly to conclude the legislative process for establishing the Dietitians Council of Nigeria. “Nutrition and dietetic practice directly affects human health and, in many cases, human life,” the institute said. He stressed that errors in clinical nutrition management could result in deteriorating health, permanent disability or death. He added that qualified dietitians and nutritionists-dietitians undertake nutritional assessments, identify nutrition-related problems, provide medical nutrition therapy and manage patients with conditions including diabetes, kidney disease, cancer and severe malnutrition. According to the institute, these responsibilities require specialised education, supervised clinical training, internship and professional competency assessments. “It is therefore dangerous to create a regulatory arrangement capable of granting professional recognition or clinical authority to persons who have not undergone the prescribed education in nutrition and dietetics, supervised clinical training, internship and professional competency assessment,” it stated. The IDN argued that establishing two councils with overlapping authority over professional education, accreditation, registration, clinical practice and disciplinary procedures would introduce uncertainty into the regulation of nutrition and dietetics in Nigeria. It warned that such an arrangement could impose additional costs on educational institutions and healthcare providers, while creating confusion over professional qualifications and the scope of practice of different categories of practitioners. The institute’s intervention comes amid a legislative debate over the appropriate regulatory structure for professionals working in nutrition and dietetics, with the proposed HB 2659 seeking to establish a separate council for nutritionists. The IDN said the existence of two statutory regulators could complicate the administration of academic programmes, particularly because many relevant courses in Nigerian tertiary institutions are organised under the integrated discipline of Nutrition and Dietetics. Ahmed said: “Most relevant academic programmes in Nigeria are established as departments or programmes of ‘Nutrition and Dietetics’. The institute warned that universities, polytechnics and colleges of health sciences and technology could face conflicting accreditation requirements, duplicated fees and uncertainty over the professional recognition of their graduates. It further cautioned that patients, employers and healthcare institutions could struggle to distinguish between professional titles such as nutritionist, registered nutritionist, clinical nutritionist, dietitian and registered dietitian. Such uncertainty, it argued, could result in clinical responsibilities being assigned to individuals without the specialised training required to perform them safely. The IDN also raised concerns about the distinction between participation in nutrition science and qualification to practise as a regulated professional.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/r.title_zh: 拒绝营养师注册委员会法案，营养研究所敦促国民议会，警告反对庸医
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/19/r.body_zh: 拟议中的委员会可能重复现有监管权力 尼日利亚饮食学研究所（IDN）敦促国民议会拒绝一项旨在设立尼日利亚营养师注册委员会的拟议法案，并警告称该法案的通过可能造成相互竞争的监管机构、削弱专业标准，并使尼日利亚人面临训练不足的从业者。该研究所支持对合格营养和饮食专业人员进行法定监管，它表示这项被确定为HB 2659的拟议立法将与2022年尼日利亚饮食师委员会（设立）法案（指定为HB 515）存在大量重叠。它呼吁众议院停止以目前形式审议HB 2659，并敦促联邦政府和国民议会完成设立尼日利亚饮食师委员会的立法程序。“营养和饮食实践直接影响人类健康，在许多情况下还影响人类生命，”该研究所表示。他强调，临床营养管理中的错误可能导致健康恶化、永久残疾或死亡。他补充说，合格的饮食师和营养师-饮食师会进行营养评估、识别与营养相关的问题、提供医学营养治疗，并管理患有糖尿病、肾脏疾病、癌症和严重营养不良等疾病的患者。根据该研究所的说法，这些职责需要专门的教育、监督下的临床培训、实习和专业能力评估。“因此，创建一个能够授予未经规定的营养和饮食教育、监督下的临床培训、实习和专业能力评估的人员以专业认可或临床权力的监管安排是危险的，”它指出。IDN认为，设立两个在专业教育、认证、注册、临床实践和纪律程序方面具有重叠权力的委员会，将给尼日利亚营养和饮食监管带来不确定性。它警告说，这种安排可能给教育机构和医疗保健提供者带来额外成本，同时造成对专业资格和不同类别从业者执业范围的混淆。该研究所的干预发生在关于营养和饮食领域专业人员适当监管结构的立法辩论之际，拟议的HB 2659寻求为营养师设立一个单独的委员会。IDN表示，两个法定监管机构的存在可能使学术项目的管理复杂化，特别是因为尼日利亚高等院校中许多相关课程是按照营养和饮食的综合学科组织的。艾哈迈德说：“尼日利亚大多数相关学术项目都是作为‘营养和饮食’系或项目设立的。”该研究所警告说，大学、理工学院和健康科学与技术学院可能面临相互冲突的认证要求、重复的费用以及对其毕业生专业认可的不确定性。它进一步警告说，患者、雇主和医疗机构可能难以区分营养师、注册营养师、临床营养师、饮食师和注册饮食师等专业头衔。它认为，这种不确定性可能导致临床职责被分配给没有所需专门培训来安全执行这些职责的个人。IDN还对参与营养科学与有资格作为受监管专业人员执业之间的区别提出了担忧。

https://dailytrust.com/information-minis.body: Deputy Senate President, Senator Jibrin Barau, Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, and governors of five states are expected at the launch of the Converged Digital Newsroom of the Media Trust Group, which is holding on Thursday, October 22, 2026, at the corporate headquarters of the company in Abuja. The Deputy Senate President will be the Special Guest of Honour at the event, while the minister will be the Guest Speaker. The Minister is expected to deliver a presentation addressing key issues surrounding media innovation, national development, and responsible journalism. Also expected to grace the unveiling of the MTG’s technology-driven initiative are governors of Yobe, Borno, Adamawa, Gombe and Jigawa states. A statement issued by the Media Trust’s management said the states were consciously chosen because of their patronage of the multimedia company. “The states are the top five customers of the company in the public sector in the 2025 Financial Year”, the statement said. Equally invited specially to the event are the management teams of Zenith Bank Plc, FirstBank Plc, the Dangote Group, Globacom Limited and Jaiz Bank Plc, which topped the list of the Media Trust Group’s customers in the private sector last year. Several other high-profile personalities, including chief executive officers of various public and private organisations are expected at the event. The MTG’s tech-driven initiative brings together editorial operations across Daily Trust, Trust TV, Trust Radio, Aminiya, Digital Trust and other platforms in a more integrated newsroom, enabling journalists to collaborate, share resources and deliver timely, relevant and engaging content to audiences across multiple channels. It also forms part of the Group’s broader strategy to build a digitally driven, audience-focused and commercially sustainable media organisation, leveraging technology and innovation to strengthen journalism and respond to the changing demands of the media industry. https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-must.body: President John Mahama has commended the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) for its contribution to the growth of gold exports, increased foreign exchange earnings and efforts to promote responsible small-scale mining. Speaking at the Mining in Motion Conference, the President highlighted an increase in gold exports from the artisanal and small-scale mining sector, alongside measures to reclaim lands destroyed by illegal mining and improve monitoring of mining equipment. “I wish to commend the Gold Board for the successes that it has chalked,” he said. President Mahama said Ghana exported 64 tonnes of gold from the artisanal and small-scale mining sector in 2024. In 2025, the country exported 104 tonnes from the sector between April and December, following the establishment of GoldBod in April. He said the regulation of small-scale gold exports had also contributed to a significant increase in foreign exchange earnings. “And I'm happy to note that the Gold Board in 2025 alone, with the regulation of export of small-scale gold, brought into this country $10.8 billion, which is an almost 100% increase over the $4.66 billion that came into the country in 2024,” he said. The President's remarks come as the government seeks to strengthen the regulation of gold trading, increase the economic benefits of the mining sector and address the environmental damage associated with illegal mining. President Mahama said the government had made progress in removing illegal miners from nine designated high-risk areas, with work now underway to prepare the affected forest reserves for reclamation. “I'm happy to note that of those nine red zones, we have cleared all of them of illegal miners and are currently preparing those forest reserves for reclamation,” he said. He said that illegal mining had destroyed approximately 12,000 acres of land across Ghana, making the restoration of affected areas a key priority. The President commended mining company Newmont for its reclamation work, saying it had restored almost 800 acres of mined-out land and planted useful crops. He also praised GoldBod for awarding the Ghana Armed Forces a contract to reclaim 253 acres of land damaged by mining activities in the Tano-Nimiri Forest. “The Gold Board has awarded the Ghana Armed Forces a contract to reclaim 253 acres of land destroyed in the famous Tano-Nimiri Forest. That work is ongoing,” he said. President Mahama further commended the Ministers of Lands and Natural Resources and Finance for allocating GH¢200 million towards the reclamation of 5,000 acres of degraded land, with the work expected to begin in 2027. The planned restoration forms part of broader efforts to repair environmental damage caused by illegal mining and protect forest reserves from further degradation. The President also outlined measures to strengthen monitoring of excavators and improve oversight of mining activities across the country. He said 6,060 excavators had been registered and detained at the ports, while 2,059 had been fitted with tracking devices to help authorities monitor their locations and use. The tracking system is intended to help the authorities identify where the equipment is being deployed and strengthen efforts to prevent its use in illegal mining operations. President Mahama also said 11 cooperatives had been trained in new mining methods and were now operational. He added that GoldBod was financing small-scale artisanal mining operations to adopt technologies designed to reduce environmental destruction. The initiative is intended to support miners in adopting improved methods while reducing the damage associated with mining activities. President Mahama said the government was also allocating funds to strengthen efforts to tackle illegal mining and protect the country's water bodies.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-must.title_zh: GoldBod必须因取得的成功而受到赞扬——马哈马
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-must.body_zh: 总统约翰·马哈马赞扬了加纳黄金局（GoldBod）对黄金出口增长、外汇收入增加以及促进负责任的小规模采矿所作出的贡献。在“采矿在进行”会议上发表讲话时，总统强调了来自手工和小规模采矿部门的黄金出口增加，以及收回被非法采矿破坏的土地和改善采矿设备监测的措施。“我想赞扬黄金局所取得的成功，”他说。马哈马总统说，加纳在2024年从手工和小规模采矿部门出口了64吨黄金。2025年，该国在4月至12月期间从该部门出口了104吨黄金，此前黄金局于4月成立。他说，小规模黄金出口的监管也为外汇收入的显著增加做出了贡献。“我很高兴地注意到，黄金局仅在2025年，通过监管小规模黄金出口，就为这个国家带来了108亿美元，这几乎是2024年进入该国的46.6亿美元的100%增长，”他说。总统的言论是在政府寻求加强黄金交易监管、增加采矿部门的经济效益并解决与非法采矿相关的环境破坏之际发表的。马哈马总统说，政府已在清除九个指定的高风险地区的非法矿工方面取得了进展，目前正在为受影响的森林保护区进行恢复准备。“我很高兴地注意到，在那九个红色区域中，我们已经清除了所有的非法矿工，目前正在为那些森林保护区进行恢复准备，”他说。他说，非法采矿已经摧毁了加纳大约12000英亩的土地，使受影响地区的恢复成为关键优先事项。总统赞扬了矿业公司Newmont的恢复工作，说它已经恢复了近800英亩的采矿土地并种植了有用的作物。他还赞扬黄金局授予加纳武装部队一份合同，以恢复在Tano-Nimiri森林中被采矿活动破坏的253英亩土地。“黄金局已授予加纳武装部队一份合同，以恢复在著名的Tano-Nimiri森林中被破坏的253英亩土地。那项工作正在进行中，”他说。马哈马总统进一步赞扬了土地和自然资源部长以及财政部长，他们拨款2亿塞地用于恢复5000英亩退化土地，预计该工作将于2027年开始。计划中的恢复是更广泛努力的一部分，旨在修复非法采矿造成的环境破坏，并保护森林保护区免受进一步退化。总统还概述了加强挖掘机监测和改善全国采矿活动监督的措施。他说，6060台挖掘机已在港口注册并被扣留，而2059台已安装了跟踪设备，以帮助当局监测它们的位置和使用情况。该跟踪系统旨在帮助当局确定设备被部署的位置，并加强防止其用于非法采矿行动的努力。马哈马总统还说，已经培训了11个合作社采用新的采矿方法，现在它们已经开始运作。他补充说，黄金局正在为小规模手工采矿作业提供资金，以采用旨在减少环境破坏的技术。该举措旨在支持矿工采用改进的方法，同时减少与采矿活动相关的破坏。马哈马总统说，政府还在拨款以加强打击非法采矿和保护该国水体的努力。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: The Cross River State Government has banned the activities of roadside mechanics and street traders in Calabar metropolis effective 31 October. The Commissioner for Environment, Bassey Mensah, disclosed this during an on-the-spot inspection of business areas, erosion sites, and other locations in Calabar on Monday. Mr Mensah said roadside technicians and traders were obstructing pedestrian and vehicular movement in the city. The commissioner also said their activities had caused serious environmental degradation in Calabar City. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that during the inspection, Mr Mensah visited Kings Street, White House, Bedwell, Punch, Victor Akan and adjoining streets. He told roadside mechanics and traders in the area to relocate their operations to designated places. “There is the possibility of exposure to harmful chemicals; we need to collectively protect public health and restore environmental order,” he said. Mr Mensah said improved sanitation is critical to creating a safe environment for residents. The commissioner expressed the government’s commitment to address environmental degradation triggered by roadside workshops and street trading. He said the state government would collaborate with the Nigeria Climate Adaptation–Erosion and Watershed Project to tackle the matter. He said the inspection was part of the ministry’s ongoing efforts to restore a clean, healthy environment in the state through improved sanitation, enforcement of environmental regulations, and sustained public sensitisation. Ndem Effiong, the senior special assistant to Governor Bassey Otu on the Automobile Technician Regulatory Department, said vehicle sales and mechanic operations need to be separated. He expressed concern about increasing environmental degradation caused by mechanics operating on the streets

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh: 克罗斯河州政府已禁止路边机械师和街头商贩在卡拉巴尔都市区的活动，该禁令自10月31日起生效。环境专员巴塞·门萨在周一对卡拉巴尔的商业区、侵蚀现场和其他地点进行现场检查时披露了这一消息。门萨先生表示，路边技师和商贩阻碍了城市中行人和车辆的通行。该专员还表示，他们的活动已导致卡拉巴尔市严重的环境退化。尼日利亚通讯社报道称，在检查期间，门萨先生走访了Kings Street、White House、Bedwell、Punch、Victor Akan及周边街道。他告诉该地区的路边机械师和商贩将他们的经营活动搬迁到指定地点。“存在接触有害化学品的可能性；我们需要共同保护公众健康并恢复环境秩序，”他说。门萨先生表示，改善卫生状况对于为居民创造安全环境至关重要。该专员表达了政府致力于解决由路边作坊和街头贸易引发的环境退化问题的决心。他说州政府将与尼日利亚气候适应-侵蚀和流域项目合作来处理此事。他说此次检查是该部通过改善卫生、执行环境法规和持续开展公众宣传来恢复该州清洁、健康环境的持续努力的一部分。Ndem Effiong是州长Bassey Otu在汽车技师监管部门的资深特别助理，他表示车辆销售和机械师操作需要分开。他对机械师在街道上作业导致的环境退化日益严重表示担忧

https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-pushe.summary: President John Dramani Mahama says Ghana is working to increase the economic benefits it derives from its gold resources by expanding local assaying, refining and related services. The initiative, being implemented through the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) and the country’s gold refining policy, is intended to deepen domestic participation in the gold value chain and reduce dependence on the extraction and export of raw minerals.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-pushe.summary_zh: 总统 John Dramani Mahama 表示，加纳正在努力通过扩大本地化验、精炼及相关服务来增加其从黄金资源中获得的经济利益。该倡议通过 Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) 和国家黄金精炼政策实施，旨在深化国内对黄金价值链的参与，并减少对原材料矿物开采和出口的依赖。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-pushe.body: President John Dramani Mahama says Ghana is working to increase the economic benefits it derives from its gold resources by expanding local assaying, refining and related services. The initiative, being implemented through the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) and the country’s gold refining policy, is intended to deepen domestic participation in the gold value chain and reduce dependence on the extraction and export of raw minerals. Addressing the Mining in Motion Conference on Monday, October 19, President Mahama underscored the importance of building local capacity to process minerals and undertake other value-added activities to ensure that more of the wealth generated from Ghana’s natural resources stays in the country. “Through the Ghana Gold Board and our gold refining policy, we are working to retain more value through assaying, refining, and related services,” he said. The policy is expected to enhance Ghana’s ability to test and refine gold domestically while creating opportunities for local businesses and professionals in the mining and mineral processing industries. The move is part of broader efforts to strengthen Ghana’s position in the gold value chain and maximise the economic returns from its mineral resources
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-pushe.title_zh: 马哈马推动本地黄金精炼以提升加纳的经济收益
https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-pushe.body_zh: 总统约翰·德拉马尼·马哈马表示，加纳正努力通过扩大本地化验、精炼及相关服务来增加从黄金资源中获得的经济利益。该举措通过加纳黄金局（GoldBod）和国家黄金精炼政策实施，旨在深化国内对黄金价值链的参与并减少对原材料矿物开采和出口的依赖。10月19日星期一在“Mining in Motion”会议上发表讲话时，马哈马总统强调了建设本地能力以加工矿物并开展其他增值活动的重要性，以确保加纳自然资源产生的更多财富留在国内。“通过加纳黄金局和我们的黄金精炼政策，我们正努力通过化验、精炼和相关服务保留更多价值，”他说。该政策有望提升加纳在国内测试和精炼黄金的能力，同时为采矿和矿物加工行业的本地企业和专业人士创造机会。此举是加强加纳在黄金价值链中地位并最大化矿产资源经济回报的更广泛努力的一部分

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: The FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, members of the Rivers State House of Assembly, and the 23 local government chairpersons in Rivers State met with Governor Siminalayi Fubara at his private residence in Port Harcourt on Sunday. The meeting comes about a fortnight after Mr Wike led members of the Rainbow Coalition in Rivers, including Kingsley Chinda, the 2027 Rivers APC governorship candidate, to meet with the governor. Although details of Sunday’s meeting were not made public, Punch newspaper reported that it was part of efforts to accommodate Mr Fubara’s camp in the emerging political structure in the state ahead of the 2027 elections. The meeting is significant because Mr Wike and the state lawmakers had been at loggerheads with Mr Fubara amid a prolonged political crisis that disrupted governance in the oil-rich state. Mr Wike, a former governor of Rivers, has intensified political engagements across the state ahead of the 2027 elections. He has held rallies and visited traditional rulers to consolidate support for President Bola Tinubu and the APC. The minister has repeatedly vowed to deliver victories for Mr Tinubu in Rivers and the FCT. The renewed reconciliation efforts come as political alignments ahead of the 2027 elections gather momentum, with former Rivers governor Rotimi Amaechi emerging as the African Democratic Congress’s vice-presidential candidate. Although some of Mr Fubara’s supporters appear reluctant to embrace the reconciliation efforts, Sunday’s meeting could signal a further attempt to bring the governor’s camp into the emerging political arrangement. However, it remains unclear how much influence Mr Fubara and his loyalists would have in the proposed arrangement. The meeting comes against the backdrop of a protracted power struggle between Mr Fubara and Mr Wike, which extended to the state legislature and local government administration. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when President Tinubu declared a state of emergency in Rivers, suspended Mr Fubara and his deputy, Ngozi Odu, as well as the state House of Assembly, and appointed a retired naval chief, Ibok-Ete Ibas, as sole administrator. During the emergency rule, Mr Ibas dissolved boards and parastatals constituted under Mr Fubara’s administration and appointed new officials, many of whom were described as loyal to Mr Wike. His administration also conducted local government elections in which Mr Wike-aligned candidates emerged as chairpersons in the state’s 23 local government areas. The emergency rule was lifted in September 2025, paving the way for Mr Fubara and other suspended elected officials to return to office. Despite the governor’s return, tensions over political control and the state government’s composition have continued to shape relations between the two camps. Mr Fubara’s cabinet remains incomplete, and he has yet to submit additional nominees to the state assembly for screening, leaving key ministries such as information without a commissioner. The reported reconciliation effort is expected to test whether the governor’s loyalists can secure a place in the state’s evolving political structure ahead of the next general elections. However, neither the details of the discussions nor the terms of any proposed political arrangement were disclosed. For now, it remains unclear whether the meeting will bring a lasting resolution to the rivalry or mark another phase in negotiations over political control in Rivers State
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh: 联邦首都区部长奈耶索姆·威克、河流州议会成员以及河流州23个地方政府主席于周日在哈科特港的私人住所与州长西米纳拉伊·富巴拉会面。此次会晤发生在威克先生率领河流州彩虹联盟成员（包括2027年河流州APC州长候选人金斯利·钦达）与州长会面大约两周之后。虽然周日会晤的细节未向公众公布，但《Punch》报纸报道称，这是为了在2027年选举前将富巴拉先生阵营纳入该州正在形成的政治结构所做努力的一部分。此次会晤意义重大，因为威克先生和州议员们曾与富巴拉先生长期对立，此前一场旷日持久的政治危机扰乱了这个石油富庶州的治理。威克先生作为河流州前州长，在2027年选举前加强了在全州范围内的政治接触。他举行了集会并访问传统统治者，以巩固对博拉·蒂努布总统和APC的支持。该部长多次发誓要在河流州和联邦首都区为蒂努布先生带来胜利。重新开始的和解努力正值2027年选举前的政治结盟势头增强之际，前河流州州长罗蒂米·阿马埃奇已作为非洲民主大会党的副总统候选人出现。尽管富巴拉先生的一些支持者似乎不愿接受和解努力，但周日的会晤可能标志着进一步尝试将州长阵营纳入正在形成的政治安排。然而，目前尚不清楚富巴拉先生及其忠诚者在拟议安排中将拥有多大影响力。此次会晤发生在富巴拉先生与威克先生之间长期权力斗争的背景下，这一斗争已延伸至州立法机构和地方政府管理。危机在2025年3月升级，当时蒂努布总统宣布河流州进入紧急状态，暂停富巴拉先生及其副手恩戈齐·奥杜以及州议会的职务，并任命退役海军将领伊博克-埃特·伊巴斯为唯一行政长官。在紧急统治期间，伊巴斯先生解散了富巴拉先生政府下设立的董事会和半官方机构，并任命了新官员，其中许多人被描述为忠于威克先生。他的政府还举行了地方政府选举，威克先生阵营的候选人在该州23个地方政府区当选为主席。紧急统治于2025年9月解除，为富巴拉先生和其他被暂停的民选官员返回办公室铺平了道路。尽管州长已返回，但围绕政治控制和州政府组成的紧张关系继续影响着两个阵营之间的关系。富巴拉先生的内阁仍不完整，他尚未向州议会提交额外提名人选进行审查，导致信息等关键部委没有专员。据报道的和解努力预计将考验州长的忠诚者是否能在下届大选前在该州不断演变的政治结构中获得一席之地。然而，讨论的细节或任何拟议政治安排的条款均未披露。目前尚不清楚此次会晤是否会为竞争带来持久解决，或标志着河流州政治控制谈判的又一阶段。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/au-commissio.title: AU Commissioner cites GoldBod as model for mineral sector reforms in Africa
https://www.myjoyonline.com/au-commissio.summary: African Union Commissioner for Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry and Minerals, Francisca Tatchououp Belobe, has pointed to Ghana’s Gold Board (GoldBod) as an example of how reforms in the mineral sector can help African countries strengthen foreign exchange reserves, support currency stability and build more resilient economies.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/au-commissio.summary_zh: 非洲联盟负责经济发展、贸易、旅游、工业和矿产的专员弗朗西斯卡·塔丘奥普·贝洛贝指出，加纳黄金局（GoldBod）是矿业部门改革如何帮助非洲国家加强外汇储备、支持货币稳定并建立更具韧性的经济的例子。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/au-commissio.body: African Union Commissioner for Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry and Minerals, Francisca Tatchououp Belobe, has pointed to Ghana’s Gold Board (GoldBod) as an example of how reforms in the mineral sector can help African countries strengthen foreign exchange reserves, support currency stability and build more resilient economies. She said the establishment of GoldBod showed how reforms in the mineral sector could support wider national development objectives, particularly through better foreign exchange management and stronger international reserves. She made the remarks at the Mining in Motion Conference on Monday, 19 October, where she said Ghana’s efforts to promote local content, strengthen domestic businesses and add value to its mineral resources offered valuable lessons for other African countries. She praised President John Dramani Mahama for Ghana’s approach and said the African Union was keen to share lessons from the initiative with other countries across the continent. According to her, Ghana’s GoldBod initiative showed how reforms in the mineral sector could contribute to broader economic objectives rather than focusing solely on the extraction and sale of natural resources. “The establishment of the Ghana Gold Board illustrates how mineral sector reform can serve broader national development objectives by improving foreign exchange, strengthening international reserves and supporting currency stability as well as macroeconomic resilience. The efforts to strengthen local content, domestic enterprises and mineral value addition also provide important lessons for other African countries,” she said. GoldBod recorded US$1.871 billion in foreign exchange from its artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold trading activities in September 2026, exceeding its monthly target of US$1.4 billion. In a release on Wednesday, September 30, the board said the foreign exchange generated had been channelled through authorised commercial banks and the Bank of Ghana to support stability in the foreign exchange market and strengthen the country’s reserves. She noted that retaining more value from mineral resources, strengthening local enterprises and improving the management of foreign exchange could help countries build stronger economic foundations
https://www.myjoyonline.com/au-commissio.title_zh: 非盟专员将GoldBod视为非洲矿业部门改革的典范
https://www.myjoyonline.com/au-commissio.body_zh: 非洲联盟经济开发、贸易、旅游、工业和矿产事务专员弗朗西斯卡·塔丘普·贝洛贝指出，加纳黄金局（GoldBod）是矿产部门改革如何帮助非洲国家加强外汇储备、支持货币稳定并构建更具韧性经济的一个例子。她说，黄金局的设立表明矿产部门改革如何能够支持更广泛的国家发展目标，特别是通过更好的外汇管理和更强大的国际储备。她是在10月19日星期一举行的‘Mining in Motion Conference’上发表上述言论的，她说加纳努力促进本地内容、加强国内企业和为其矿产资源增加价值，为其他非洲国家提供了宝贵经验。她赞扬约翰·德拉马尼·马哈马总统对加纳采取的方法，并表示非洲联盟渴望与非洲大陆其他国家分享这一举措的经验。根据她的说法，加纳的黄金局举措表明矿产部门改革如何能够为更广泛的经济目标做出贡献，而不仅仅是专注于自然资源的开采和销售。“加纳黄金局的设立表明，矿产部门改革如何能够通过改善外汇、加强国际储备、支持货币稳定以及宏观经济韧性来服务于更广泛的国家发展目标。加强本地内容、国内企业和矿产价值增加的努力也为其他非洲国家提供了重要经验，”她说。黄金局在2026年9月的个体和小型采矿（ASM）黄金交易活动中录得18.71亿美元的外汇，超过了其每月14亿美元的目标。在9月30日星期三的一份声明中，该局表示所产生的外汇已通过授权的商业银行和加纳银行引导，以支持外汇市场的稳定并加强该国的储备。她指出，从矿产资源中保留更多价值、加强本地企业和改善外汇管理可以帮助各国建立更强大的经济基础

https://www.myjoyonline.com/vice-preside.summary: Vice-President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged Chinese investors to invest in Ghana’s local processing and manufacturing industries as part of efforts to accelerate industrialisation, create jobs and derive greater economic value from the country’s natural resources.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/vice-preside.summary_zh: 副总统纳安娜·简·奥波库-阿吉曼教授敦促中国投资者投资加纳本地加工和制造业，以此作为加速工业化、创造就业机会并从国家自然资源中获得更大经济价值的努力的一部分。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/vice-preside.body: Vice-President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged Chinese investors to invest in Ghana’s local processing and manufacturing industries as part of efforts to accelerate industrialisation, create jobs and derive greater economic value from the country’s natural resources. Speaking to Chinese business executives in Shanghai, she outlined investment opportunities in cocoa, shea nuts, cashew nuts, coconut, timber and other raw materials, encouraging investors to support the production of finished and semi-finished goods from these commodities. She emphasised that Ghana needed to reduce its reliance on raw material exports by building a strong manufacturing sector that could generate employment, enhance productivity and retain a greater proportion of economic value within the country. Professor Opoku-Agyemang pointed to timber processing as an area with significant potential, explaining that Ghana could secure better returns by producing furniture and other finished wood products instead of exporting logs. She said greater investment in domestic processing would strengthen industrial development while providing sustainable employment opportunities for the country’s growing population. The Vice-President further highlighted the importance of ensuring that technical and vocational education and training meets the needs of industry, enabling young people to acquire skills that correspond with available employment opportunities. “Training people for jobs that do not exist is training them for unemployment,” she said. She explained that investment in productive sectors was necessary to create opportunities for technically trained young people to put their skills to use and contribute to national development. She cautioned that a lack of adequate employment opportunities could leave increasing numbers of trained young people frustrated. Professor Opoku-Agyemang reiterated Ghana’s willingness to work with Chinese businesses through mutually beneficial partnerships, particularly in manufacturing, logistics and other productive areas that could contribute to sustainable economic growth. She also drew attention to the opportunities available through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which provides a framework for increasing trade across Africa. According to her, Ghana’s strategic location as a gateway to the wider African market presents an opportunity for Chinese investors to establish businesses that can reach customers across the continent. She nevertheless stressed that partnerships between Ghana and China should produce practical benefits for both countries, including employment creation, increased productive capacity and improved opportunities for Ghanaian businesses. The Vice-President also questioned the extent of Ghanaian traders’ participation in businesses associated with China, raising concerns about the opportunities available to them in the Chinese market. In particular, she questioned whether Ghanaian traders could obtain ownership stakes in the businesses they support. Her concerns highlighted the need for stronger participation by Ghanaian entrepreneurs in international trade and investment, ensuring that economic cooperation between the two countries provides opportunities for local businesses to benefit more directly. The discussions form part of Ghana’s wider efforts to strengthen economic relations with China and attract investment into industries capable of adding value to the country’s raw materials. Ghana produces commodities including cocoa, cashew nuts, shea and timber, alongside mineral resources such as bauxite, lithium and diamonds. Increasing investment in domestic processing and manufacturing could help create employment, develop local industries, reduce dependence on raw material exports and ensure that a larger share of the value generated from these resources remains in Ghana.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/vice-preside.title_zh: 副总统呼吁中国投资加纳原材料的本地加工
https://www.myjoyonline.com/vice-preside.body_zh: 副总统纳安娜·简·奥波库-阿吉曼教授敦促中国投资者投资加纳本地加工和制造业，以此作为加速工业化、创造就业机会并从国家自然资源中获取更大经济价值的努力的一部分。她在上海对中国企业高管讲话时，概述了可可、乳木果、腰果、椰子、木材和其他原材料的投资机会，鼓励投资者支持用这些商品生产成品和半成品。她强调，加纳需要通过建立强大的制造业来减少对原材料出口的依赖，该制造业能够创造就业、提高生产力并在国内保留更大比例的经济价值。奥波库-阿吉曼教授指出木材加工是一个具有巨大潜力的领域，她解释说，加纳可以通过生产家具和其他成品木制品而不是出口原木来获得更好的回报。她表示，对国内加工的更大投资将加强工业发展，同时为国家不断增长的人口提供可持续的就业机会。副总统进一步强调，确保技术和职业教育与培训满足行业需求的重要性，这能让年轻人获得与现有就业机会相匹配的技能。“为不存在的工作培训人们就是培训他们失业，”她说。她解释说，对生产性部门的投资对于为受过技术培训的年轻人创造机会来运用他们的技能并为国家发展做出贡献是必要的。她警告说，缺乏足够的就业机会可能会让越来越多受过培训的年轻人感到沮丧。奥波库-阿吉曼教授重申了加纳愿意通过互利伙伴关系与中国企业合作，特别是在制造业、物流和其他能够促进可持续经济增长的生产性领域。她还提请注意通过非洲大陆自由贸易区（AfCFTA）提供的机会，该自贸区为增加非洲内部贸易提供了框架。据她介绍，加纳作为通往更广阔非洲市场的门户的战略位置为中国投资者提供了一个机会，可以建立能够触及整个非洲大陆客户的企业。尽管如此，她强调，加纳和中国之间的伙伴关系应该为两国带来实际利益，包括创造就业、提高生产能力和改善加纳企业的机会。副总统还质疑加纳贸易商参与与中国相关业务的程度，对他们在中国的市场中可获得的机会表示担忧。她特别质疑加纳贸易商是否能够获得他们所支持企业的所有权股份。她的担忧突显了加纳企业家需要更强地参与国际贸易和投资，确保两国之间的经济合作能为本地企业提供更直接的受益机会。这些讨论是加纳加强与中国经济关系并吸引投资进入能够为国家原材料增加价值的产业的更广泛努力的一部分。加纳生产包括可可、腰果、乳木果和木材在内的商品，以及铝土矿、锂和钻石等矿产资源。增加对国内加工和制造业的投资可以帮助创造就业、发展本地产业、减少对原材料出口的依赖，并确保这些资源产生的更大份额的价值留在加纳。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: Eight members of the Zamfara State House of Assembly who recently resigned from the All Progressives Congress (APC) have announced their return to the party. This development followed a meeting with President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. The legislators were led to the meeting by the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, alongside Aminu Jaji, who represents the Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives. The lawmakers are Aliyu Kagara (Talata Mafara South), Ibrahim Tukur (Bakura), Faruk Dosara (Maradun I), Bashir Masama (Bukkuyum North), Muktaru Kaura (Kaura North), Nasiru Abdullahi (Maru North), Bashar Bello (Bungudu West), and Bashar Aliyu (Gummi I). They had been widely tipped to defect to the African Democratic Congress (ADC) after announcing their resignation from the APC, citing internal party friction and escalating security challenges in rural Zamfara communities. They also alleged non-payment of certain allowances and entitlements by the assembly. The lawmakers had been embroiled in a protracted power struggle in the State House of Assembly. They were suspended by the Assembly leadership for attempting to remove the Speaker. However, they have now stated that their grievances were being addressed through presidential reconciliation championed by Mr Matawalle. The lawmakers promised to work for the growth of the party and its victory in the 2027 elections. However, one of them, Mr Abdullahi (Maru North), has been screened to contest for the state legislature seat under the ADC. Zamfara is one of Nigeria’s most politically volatile states, currently governed by Dauda Lawal, who defected earlier this year from the PDP, having defeated the sitting APC governor, Mr Matawalle, in the 2023 governorship election. The state APC hierarchy has experienced persistent factional tensions among key party figures, including former governors Mr Matawalle and Abdul’aziz Yari, as well as federal lawmakers like Mr Jaji. President Tinubu’s intervention is seen by political analysts as a critical move to unite the party for the 2027 elections
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 2027年：八名赞法拉州议员转变立场，在会见蒂努布后准备重返APC
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 最近从全体进步大会党（APC）辞职的赞法拉州议会八名议员宣布重返该党。这一事态发展是在阿布贾总统别墅与总统博拉·蒂努布会面后发生的。这些议员由国防国务部长贝洛·马塔瓦莱率领，与代表众议院考拉·纳莫达/比尔宁·马加吉联邦选区的阿米努·贾吉一同参加会议。议员包括阿里尤·卡加拉（塔拉塔·马法拉南）、易卜拉欣·图库尔（巴库拉）、法鲁克·多萨拉（马拉敦一）、巴希尔·马萨马（布库尤姆北）、穆克塔鲁·考拉（考拉北）、纳西鲁·阿卜杜拉希（马鲁北）、巴沙尔·贝洛（本古杜西）和巴沙尔·阿里尤（古米一）。他们在宣布从APC辞职后，曾被广泛认为将转投非洲民主大会党（ADC），理由是党内摩擦以及赞法拉农村社区安全挑战升级。他们还指控议会未支付某些津贴和应享权利。这些议员曾卷入州议会旷日持久的权力斗争。他们因试图罢免议长而被议会领导层停职。然而，他们现在表示，他们的不满正通过马塔瓦莱先生推动的总统和解得到解决。这些议员承诺为该党的发展和在2027年选举中的胜利而努力。不过，其中一位阿卜杜拉希先生（马鲁北）已接受筛查，将以ADC身份竞选州议会席位。赞法拉是尼日利亚政治最动荡的州之一，目前由达乌达·拉瓦尔执政，他今年早些时候从人民民主党（PDP）转党，在2023年州长选举中击败了时任APC州长马塔瓦莱先生。该州APC领导层在包括前州长马塔瓦莱先生和阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·亚里以及联邦议员如贾吉先生等关键党派人物之间一直存在持续的派系紧张。政治分析人士认为，蒂努布总统的干预是团结该党以备2027年选举的关键举措。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body: Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) enjoys broad support in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, citing Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Nyesom Wike’s backing for President Bola Tinubu. Mr AbdulRazaq made the statement on Sunday in Ilorin while receiving a delegation of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), led by its Director-General, Abdulaziz Yari. The governor dismissed the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) as a weakened political force in Kwara. He argued that Mr Wike’s support for Mr Tinubu could further strengthen the APC’s electoral position. “The balance of the equation here is 70-30: 70 per cent APC and 30 per cent PDP. And that’s consistent from 2019 until the election. Nothing has changed except that the PDP has continued to weaken,” Mr AbdulRazaq said. He added that Mr Wike’s position could change the political calculations ahead of the elections. “With the national leader of the PDP being a member of our campaign council and declaring that his party, the PDP, will vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, it means that the PDP 30 per cent versus our 70 per cent is now adding up to 100 per cent,” he said. The governor’s projection was not accompanied by independent polling data to substantiate the claimed support percentages. Mr Wike’s support for Mr Tinubu has persisted despite his disagreements with some APC governors, including Mr AbdulRazaq. During a media chat in Port Harcourt on 2 September, the minister accused the Kwara governor of leading a campaign against him and said he had confronted him over the alleged hostility. The disagreement is linked to Mr Wike’s relationships with aggrieved APC figures in Kwara, some of whom oppose the governor’s preferred candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. The Wike-led PDP’s governorship candidate, Suleiman Kawu, is supported by some of the aggrieved APC figures, including sitting Kwara Central District senator, Salihu Mustapha, who is seeking reelection as the PDP candidate. Mr AbdulRazaq expressed confidence in the APC’s Kwara governorship candidate, Salihu Yakubu Danladi, the Speaker of the state House of Assembly, saying his legislative experience had given him an understanding of the state’s budget and government operations. The governor defended his administration’s record since the APC took office in 2019, citing developments in education, healthcare and the civil service. “When we came in 2019, it was a challenging situation. Salaries were not paid, gratuities were not paid, pensions were not paid. That is a thing of the past,” he said. Mr Yari said the delegation visited Kwara to seek the governor’s continued support for the APC’s nationwide campaign. The delegation included former governors Abdullahi Ganduje, Olusegun Mimiko, Ali Modu Sheriff, Rochas Okorocha, Aminu Bello Masari, Adamu Badaru, Ibrahim Shema, Sani Yerima, Danjuma Goje and Abubakar Aleiro, as well as APC National Secretary Ajibola Basiru. Former Speaker of the House of Representatives Dimeji Bankole and former lawmaker Olubunmi Ette were also among those present. The delegation, accompanied by Mr AbdulRazaq, later visited the Emir of Ilorin and Chairman of the Kwara State Council of Chiefs, Ibrahim Sulu-Gambari, at his palace to pay homage and seek prayers ahead of the 2027 elections. The visit comes amid internal disagreements within the Kwara APC over the party’s governorship ticket. PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that a group identifying itself as the Kwara State APC Elders Caucus rejected Mr Danladi’s emergence as the party’s governorship candidate and urged the national leadership to revisit the outcome of the 22 May primary. The party dismissed the group’s position, insisting that the primary was validly conducted.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.title_zh: 2027年：阿卜杜勒拉扎克预测APC在夸拉州获胜，引用威克对蒂努布的支持
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body_zh: 夸拉州州长阿卜杜勒拉赫曼·阿卜杜勒拉扎克表示，在2027年大选之前，全进步大会党（APC）在该州享有广泛支持，并引用联邦首都区（FCT）部长奈耶索姆·维克对总统博拉·蒂努布的支持。阿卜杜勒拉扎克先生周日在伊洛林发表上述言论，当时他正在接待由其总干事阿卜杜拉齐兹·亚里领导的全进步大会党总统竞选委员会（PCC）代表团。州长认为人民民主党（PDP）在夸拉已是一支削弱的政治力量。他认为维克先生对蒂努布先生的支持可能进一步加强全进步大会党的选举地位。“这里的平衡方程式是70-30：70%属于全进步大会党，30%属于人民民主党。这从2019年一直到选举都是一致的。除了人民民主党继续削弱之外，没有任何变化，”阿卜杜勒拉扎克先生说。他补充说，维克先生的立场可能会改变选举前的政治计算。“随着人民民主党的全国领袖成为我们竞选委员会的成员，并宣布他的政党人民民主党将投票支持总统博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布，这意味着人民民主党的30%加上我们的70%现在总计达到100%，”他说。州长的预测并未附带独立民调数据来证实所声称的支持百分比。尽管维克先生与包括阿卜杜勒拉扎克先生在内的一些全进步大会党州长存在分歧，但他对蒂努布先生的支持一直持续。在9月2日哈科特港的一次媒体聊天中，该部长指责夸拉州州长领导了一场针对他的竞选活动，并表示他已就所谓的敌对行为与他当面对质。这一分歧与维克先生与夸拉州不满的全进步大会党人士的关系有关，其中一些人反对州长在2027年选举前偏好的候选人。由维克领导的人民民主党州长候选人苏莱曼·卡武得到一些不满的全进步大会党人士的支持，包括现任夸拉中央区参议员萨利胡·穆斯塔法，他正寻求作为人民民主党候选人连任。阿卜杜勒拉扎克先生对全进步大会党夸拉州州长候选人、州议会发言人萨利胡·雅库布·丹拉迪表示有信心，说他的立法经验使他了解了该州的预算和政府运作。州长为自全进步大会党2019年执政以来其政府的记录辩护，引用了教育、医疗和公务员系统的进展。“当我们2019年上任时，情况具有挑战性。工资没有支付，慰问金没有支付，养老金没有支付。那已成为过去，”他说。亚里先生表示，代表团访问夸拉是为了寻求州长继续支持全进步大会党在全国范围的竞选活动。代表团包括前州长阿卜杜拉希·甘杜杰、奥卢塞贡·米米科、阿里·莫杜·谢里夫、罗查斯·奥科罗查、阿米努·贝洛·马萨里、阿达穆·巴达鲁、易卜拉欣·谢马、萨尼·耶里马、丹朱马·戈杰和阿布巴卡尔·阿莱罗，以及全进步大会党全国书记阿吉博拉·巴西鲁。前众议院议长迪梅吉·班科莱和前议员奥卢本米·埃特也在出席者之列。代表团在阿卜杜勒拉扎克先生的陪同下，随后前往伊洛林埃米尔兼夸拉州酋长委员会主席易卜拉欣·苏鲁-甘巴里的宫殿致敬，并在2027年选举前寻求祈祷。此次访问是在夸拉全进步大会党内部就该党的州长候选人资格存在分歧之际进行的。PREMIUM TIMES此前报道称，一个自称为夸拉州全进步大会党长老核心小组的团体拒绝丹拉迪先生成为该党州长候选人的结果，并敦促全国领导层重新审议5月22日初选的结果。该党驳斥了该团体的立场，坚持认为初选是有效进行的。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title: NLNG Dividends: Oyo govt challenges presidency to explain distribution of $3bn received under Tinubu
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary: The dispute followed Mr Makinde’s claim that each state was entitled to about N250 billion in NLNG dividends that had allegedly been withheld by the federal government. The presidency said NLNG had paid approximately $21.5 billion in dividends to the federation over the past 25 years, with less than $3 billion received under the Tinubu administration.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary_zh: 争议源于马金德先生声称每个州有权获得约2500亿奈拉的NLNG分红，据称这些分红被联邦政府扣留。总统府表示，NLNG在过去25年中已向联邦支付约215亿美元的分红，其中在蒂努布政府领导下收到的不到30亿美元。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media, Sulaimon Olanrewaju, Mr Makinde said the presidency’s response failed to address the central question of how the funds were distributed. The governor, the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement for the 2027 election, said the Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF), with the federal government’s support, engaged a consultant to reconcile NLNG dividend payments. “The exercise identified a shortfall of about N9 trillion due to states and local governments. The federal government accepted the findings,” the statement read. Mr Makinde added that the reconciliation report remained in the custody of both the federal government and the NGF, expressing confidence that the presidency would not deny its existence. The governor, who will be running against President Tinubu, the candidate of the All Progressives Congress in the upcoming 2027 election, is the incumbent vice-chairman of the NGF. The dispute followed Mr Makinde’s claim that each state was entitled to about N250 billion in NLNG dividends that had allegedly been withheld by the federal government. In its response on Sunday, presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga described the claim as false, arguing that the amount would imply a total distribution of N9 trillion to the 36 states alone. Mr Onanuga said states receive 26.72 per cent of distributable Federation Account revenue under the existing revenue-sharing formula. He argued that for the states’ combined share to reach N9 trillion, total NLNG dividends paid into the Federation Account would have to exceed N33.68 trillion ($25 billion), in a single declaration. The presidency said NLNG had paid approximately $21.5 billion in dividends to the federation over the past 25 years, with less than $3 billion received under the Tinubu administration. The Oyo government said the presidency had not explained how the dividends received under the current administration were distributed or how much each tier of government received. “Have states and local governments received their shares? How much did they receive, and how were those amounts calculated? What happened to the $3 billion received under this administration?” the statement asked. The statement also defended Mr Makinde’s figures, saying the governor had a basis for his claims. “Governor Makinde conducts public discourse with decorum and does not make unfounded claims or quote figures without a basis.” It urged the presidency to address the substance of the allegation and said it was ready to provide further clarification
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: NLNG分红：奥约州政府要求总统府解释在蒂努布领导下收到的30亿美元分配情况
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 在他的媒体特别顾问苏莱曼·奥兰雷瓦朱发表的一份声明中，马金德先生表示，总统府的回应未能解决资金如何分配的核心问题。这位州长、2027年选举中人民联盟运动的总统候选人表示，尼日利亚州长论坛（NGF）在联邦政府的支持下，聘请了一名顾问来核对NLNG的股息支付。“该行动发现各州和地方政府存在约9万亿奈拉的短缺。联邦政府接受了这些调查结果，”声明写道。马金德先生补充说，和解报告仍由联邦政府和尼日利亚州长论坛共同保管，他表示相信总统府不会否认其存在。这位州长将在即将到来的2027年选举中与进步大会党候选人蒂努布总统竞争，他是尼日利亚州长论坛的现任副主席。这场争端源于马金德先生声称每个州有权获得约2500亿奈拉的NLNG股息，据称这些股息被联邦政府扣留。在周日的回应中，总统发言人巴约·奥纳努加称这一说法是虚假的，认为这一数额将意味着仅向36个州就总共分配9万亿奈拉。奥纳努加先生表示，根据现有的收入分享公式，各州获得可分配联邦账户收入的26.72%。他辩称，要使各州合计份额达到9万亿奈拉，支付到联邦账户的NLNG股息总额必须超过33.68万亿奈拉（250亿美元），这是在单次申报中的情况。总统府表示，NLNG在过去25年中已向联邦支付约215亿美元的股息，在蒂努布政府期间收到的不到30亿美元。奥约州政府表示，总统府没有解释当前政府期间收到的股息是如何分配的，或者各级政府各自收到了多少。“各州和地方政府是否收到了他们的份额？他们收到了多少，这些金额是如何计算的？本届政府收到的30亿美元发生了什么？”声明问道。该声明还为马金德先生的数字进行了辩护，称州长有依据提出他的主张。“马金德州长以礼貌的方式进行公共讨论，不会提出毫无根据的主张或在没有依据的情况下引用数字。”它敦促总统府回应指控的实质内容，并表示准备提供进一步澄清。

https://leadership.ng/federal-government.summary: The federal government, through the Bank of Industry (BOI) and the Federal Ministry of Youth Development (FMYD), has launched a pilot empowerment programme offering free vocational and entrepreneurial training to 500 young Nigerians. The BOI Youth Empowerment Pilot Programme, announced in Lagos will be delivered by Sapphital, a Pan-African digital learning and technology company based in Abuja.
https://leadership.ng/federal-government.summary_zh: 联邦政府通过工业银行（BOI）和联邦青年发展部（FMYD）启动了一项试点赋权计划，为500名尼日利亚青年提供免费职业和创业培训。该BOI青年赋权试点计划在拉各斯宣布，将由Sapphital交付，这是一家总部位于阿布贾的泛非数字学习和技术公司。
https://leadership.ng/federal-government.body: The federal government, through the Bank of Industry (BOI) and the Federal Ministry of Youth Development (FMYD), has launched a pilot empowerment programme offering free vocational and entrepreneurial training to 500 young Nigerians. The BOI Youth Empowerment Pilot Programme, announced in Lagos will be delivered by Sapphital, a Pan-African digital learning and technology company based in Abuja. Sapphital specialises in AI-powered Learning Management Systems (LMS), e-learning and custom software solutions. The training will be delivered through the Nigerian Youth Academy (NiYA), where participants will complete short, instructor-led video courses. The courses were carefully selected based on income-generation potential and market demand, covering creative and artisan skills, production and manufacturing skills, as well as digital skills. In addition to the core training, selected participants will have access to mentorship, practical exposure and enterprise support opportunities to help them transition into employment or entrepreneurship. Speaking on the launch, the Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to youth empowerment. “President Bola Tinubu believes that youth empowerment and training are core pillars of national reform. A nation succeeds when its young population are globally competitive. Through this programme, we hope to equip Nigerian youths with the skills and capabilities they need to compete and thrive on a global scale,” Olawande said. Speaking on the programme, the managing director and chief executive officer of the Bank of Industry, Dr. Olasupo Olusi described young Nigerians as the country’s greatest economic asset. “Young Nigerians are our greatest economic asset, and the Bank of Industry is committed to providing them the tools required to build a brighter future, creating viable enterprises. This pilot is much more than just a training programme. It connects young people to skills, mentorship and real opportunities to start and sustain businesses,” Olusi said. “Through our partnership with the Federal Ministry of Youth Development and Sapphital, we are building a model that can be scaled across Nigeria to reach even more young people in support of the Renewed Hope Agenda,” he added. https://leadership.ng/timi-frank-seeks-t.title: Timi Frank Seeks Trump’s Help Over Alleged Threat To Atiku’s Safety
https://leadership.ng/timi-frank-seeks-t.summary: Frank, in an open letter addressed to Trump and other international leaders on Monday, expressed concern over reports of alleged plans to intimidate, arrest, detain or otherwise undermine Atiku’s participation in the forthcoming electoral process.
https://leadership.ng/timi-frank-seeks-t.summary_zh: 弗兰克周一在一封致特朗普和其他国际领导人的公开信中，对有关据称计划恐吓、逮捕、拘留或以其他方式破坏阿蒂库参与即将到来的选举进程的报道表示担忧。
https://leadership.ng/timi-frank-seeks-t.body: Frank, in an open letter addressed to Trump and other international leaders on Monday, expressed concern over reports of alleged plans to intimidate, arrest, detain or otherwise undermine Atiku’s participation in the forthcoming electoral process. Atiku, a leading opposition figure and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has been at the centre of political debates ahead of the 2027 elections. Frank urged the United States, the United Nations, the African Union (AU), the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the European Union (EU) and the United Kingdom to engage the Nigerian government and demand credible assurances regarding the safety of opposition leaders. According to Frank, who serves as an ambassador of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua (ULMWP) to East Africa and the Middle East, the allegations concerning Atiku’s safety and the possible use of state institutions against opposition figures require urgent and independent investigation. “These allegations must be independently and urgently investigated. Given their gravity, however, they cannot be dismissed or ignored until it is too late to prevent harm,” he said. Frank warned that any attempt to use law enforcement or security agencies to obstruct opposition candidates would undermine democratic participation and erode public confidence in Nigeria’s institutions. “The protection of political opposition is not a favour that any government grants at its discretion. It is a fundamental obligation of every democratic state,” he said. He specifically raised concerns over allegations that the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) could be used to initiate proceedings against Atiku under circumstances that might lead to his arrest and prolonged detention during the election campaign. However, Frank clarified that his position was not that political figures should be exempt from legitimate investigations, but that law enforcement agencies must operate independently and without political interference. “The concern is not that Atiku Abubakar should be placed above the law. The concern is that the law must never be placed at the service of political persecution,” he said. He called on the Federal Government to ensure that any investigation involving opposition figures was based on credible evidence and conducted in accordance with due process. Frank also questioned the perceived selective application of anti-corruption laws, arguing that public confidence in institutions such as the EFCC depended on their ability to investigate allegations impartially, regardless of political affiliation. He maintained that no public official or political associate should be shielded from legitimate scrutiny because of proximity to the presidency. “If the government expects Nigerians to trust its anti-corruption institutions, those institutions must demonstrate that justice is neither partisan nor selective,” he said. Describing Atiku as one of Nigeria’s most prominent opposition figures, Frank said his criticism of government policies and participation in debates on governance and public accountability were legitimate features of a democratic system. He argued that political disagreements should be addressed through open debate and lawful procedures rather than intimidation or threats. “The test of Nigeria’s democracy is not whether the government protects its allies, but whether it protects the rights of those who challenge it,” Frank added. Frank also expressed concern about the credibility of the 2027 general elections, urging the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and the judiciary to demonstrate impartiality in the discharge of their responsibilities. He said allegations of restrictions on opposition campaigns, political intimidation and interference with electoral institutions should be independently investigated before they escalate.
https://leadership.ng/timi-frank-seeks-t.title_zh: Timi Frank寻求特朗普帮助，称Atiku安全受到威胁
https://leadership.ng/timi-frank-seeks-t.body_zh: 弗兰克周一在一封致特朗普和其他国际领导人的公开信中，对有关据称计划恐吓、逮捕、拘留或以其他方式破坏阿蒂库参与即将到来的选举进程的报道表示担忧。阿蒂库作为主要反对派人物和非洲民主大会党（ADC）的总统候选人，在2027年选举前一直处于政治辩论的中心。弗兰克敦促美国、联合国、非洲联盟（AU）、西非国家经济共同体（ECOWAS）、欧洲联盟（EU）和联合王国与尼日利亚政府接触，并要求就反对派领导人的安全问题提供可信的保证。据作为西巴布亚联合解放运动（ULMWP）驻东非和中东大使的弗兰克称，有关阿蒂库安全以及可能利用国家机构对付反对派人物的指控需要进行紧急和独立的调查。“这些指控必须独立且紧急地进行调查。然而，鉴于其严重性，在为时已晚无法防止伤害之前，它们不能被驳回或忽视，”他说。弗兰克警告说，任何试图利用执法或安全机构阻挠反对派候选人的行为都将破坏民主参与并削弱公众对尼日利亚机构的信心。“保护政治反对派不是任何政府自行决定的恩惠。它是每个民主国家的一项基本义务，”他说。他特别对有关经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）可能被用来在可能导致阿蒂库在选举竞选期间被捕和长期拘留的情况下启动针对阿蒂库的程序的指控表示担忧。然而，弗兰克澄清说，他的立场并非政治人物应免于合法调查，而是执法机构必须独立运作且不受政治干预。“问题不是阿蒂库·阿布巴卡尔应该凌驾于法律之上。问题是法律绝不能被置于为政治迫害服务的地位，”他说。他呼吁联邦政府确保任何涉及反对派人物的调查都基于可信证据并按照正当程序进行。弗兰克还质疑反腐败法律被认为的选择性适用，他认为公众对EFCC等机构的信心取决于它们无论政治派别如何都能公正调查指控的能力。他坚持认为，任何公职人员或政治伙伴都不应因与总统的关系而免于合法审查。“如果政府期望尼日利亚人信任其反腐败机构，这些机构必须证明正义既非党派也非选择性的，”他说。弗兰克将阿蒂库描述为尼日利亚最杰出的反对派人物之一，他说他对政府政策的批评以及参与关于治理和公共问责的辩论是民主制度的合法特征。他认为，政治分歧应通过公开辩论和合法程序来解决，而不是通过恐吓或威胁。“尼日利亚民主的考验不是政府是否保护其盟友，而是它是否保护那些挑战它的人的权利，”弗兰克补充说。弗兰克还对2027年大选的可信度表示担忧，敦促独立国家选举委员会（INEC）、安全机构和司法机构在履行职责时表现出公正性。他说，有关限制反对派竞选、政治恐吓和干预选举机构的指控应在升级之前进行独立调查。

https://leadership.ng/matawalle-leads-8-.body: Eight suspended members of the Zamfara State House of Assembly who recently resigned from the All Progressives Congress (APC) have met with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, reaffirming their loyalty to the party. The lawmakers were led to the Presidential Villa by the Minister of State for Defence and former Governor of Zamfara State, Dr. Bello Matawalle. A statement by Matawalle’s Personal Assistant on Media, Ahmad Dan-Wudil, on Monday said the lawmakers reaffirmed their support for President Tinubu and their resolve to remain in the APC. According to the statement, Matawalle pledged to integrate the lawmakers into the Tinubu Again Movement (TAM) to work collectively for President Tinubu and all APC candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. The lawmakers are Aliyu Ango Kagara (Talata Mafara South), Ibrahim Tukur Bakura (Bakura), Faruk Musa Dosara (Maradun I), Bashir Abubakar Masama (Bukkuyum North), Muktaru Nasiru Kaura (Kaura North), Nasiru Abdullahi (Maru North), Bashar Bello (Bungudu West), and Bashar Aliyu (Gummi I). LEADERSHIP recalls that the eight lawmakers were suspended on February 26, 2024, over allegations of gross misconduct, conspiracy and holding an illegal sitting. The suspension was extended on May 13, 2026. The Speaker of the Zamfara State House of Assembly, Bilyaminu Ismail Moriki, had said the suspension predated their political decision and arose from disciplinary matters within the House. The lawmakers had in their resignation letters cited alleged injustice, disunity among APC stakeholders in the state and the handling of insecurity as reasons for leaving the party. An APC chieftain, Dr. Sani Shinkafi, had clarified that five of the eight legislators were elected in 2023 on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) before defecting to the APC, while only three won their seats on the APC ticket. https://leadership.ng/fg-targets-1m-cng-.summary: Ekpo said the government must ensure that its autogas policy delivers tangible benefits to Nigerians, particularly by reducing transport fares following the removal of the petrol subsidy in 2023. However, the extent to which it can reduce transport fares depends on the availability of refuelling stations, affordable vehicle conversions, reliable gas supply and whether operators pass their fuel savings on to passengers.
https://leadership.ng/fg-targets-1m-cng-.summary_zh: 埃克波说，政府必须确保其汽车燃气政策为尼日利亚人带来切实利益，特别是在2023年取消汽油补贴后降低交通费用。然而，它能在多大程度上降低交通费用取决于加油站的可用性、负担得起的车辆改装、可靠的燃气供应以及运营商是否将他们的燃料节省传递给乘客。
https://leadership.ng/fg-targets-1m-cng-.body: The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, gave the directive in Abuja over the weekend while receiving progress reports from the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles and the Decade of Gas Secretariat. Ekpo said the government must ensure that its autogas policy delivers tangible benefits to Nigerians, particularly by reducing transport fares following the removal of the petrol subsidy in 2023. According to a statement issued on Sunday by the minister’s spokesman, Louis Ibah, Ekpo tasked the leadership of the two bodies with identifying critical interventions, expanding infrastructure and strengthening programmes to increase the nationwide adoption of CNG. The statement said the government would intensify efforts to promote CNG as a cheaper alternative fuel for transportation, with renewed emphasis on accelerating the deployment of one million gas-powered vehicles across the country. The renewed push comes amid persistent concerns over rising public transportation costs since the removal of the petrol subsidy, which increased fuel expenses for commercial transport operators and added pressure on household incomes. CNG has been promoted by the federal government as an alternative to petrol because it is generally cheaper on an energy-equivalent basis. However, the extent to which it can reduce transport fares depends on the availability of refuelling stations, affordable vehicle conversions, reliable gas supply and whether operators pass their fuel savings on to passengers. Ekpo said Nigeria’s abundant natural gas reserves presented an opportunity to reduce transportation costs, increase domestic gas consumption and stimulate economic growth. “Nigeria is a gas nation with a gas reserves index of over 80 yrs, and that is why we are talking about the Decade(s) of Gas,” he said. The minister stressed the need to implement President Bola Tinubu’s directive to make transportation more affordable through CNG, assuring officials of the government’s continued support. “It is important that we listen to the directive of Mr President to make transportation cheaper via CNG. We will continue to give you all the backing to provide the necessary assistance to make sure we drive this project to a logical conclusion,” Ekpo said. He urged the Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles and the Decade of Gas Secretariat to sustain investments in refuelling infrastructure, vehicle conversion facilities and other essential components required to expand the use of natural gas as a transportation fuel. Ekpo also welcomed progress recorded under the current leadership of the Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles, reiterating the government’s commitment to supporting the programme. He further disclosed that domestic gas consumption had risen above two billion cubic feet per day for the first time in Nigeria’s history, describing the development as an opportunity to deepen gas utilisation and advance the country’s economic ambitions. The chairman of the Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles, Ismaeel Ahmed, said the initiative would intensify investments and programmes to expand refuelling infrastructure and increase the number of vehicles converted to run on gas. Ahmed said the effort was designed to make CNG more accessible to transport operators and help reduce fares for millions of Nigerians. He added that a joint industry market study completed by the Decade of Gas Secretariat had provided a framework for accelerating the rollout, monitoring progress, identifying infrastructure gaps and improving implementation. According to him, the study would help the government and industry stakeholders determine priority interventions and strengthen efforts to make CNG widely available as a transportation fuel.
https://leadership.ng/fg-targets-1m-cng-.title_zh: 联邦政府目标实现100万辆压缩天然气汽车以降低交通费用
https://leadership.ng/fg-targets-1m-cng-.body_zh: 石油资源国务部长（天然气），埃克佩里克佩·埃克波，周末在阿布贾接收总统压缩天然气和电动汽车倡议以及天然气十年秘书处的进展报告时下达了这一指令。埃克波表示，政府必须确保其汽车燃气政策为尼日利亚人带来切实利益，特别是在2023年取消汽油补贴后通过降低交通费用来实现这一点。根据部长发言人路易斯·伊巴赫周日发布的声明，埃克波责成这两个机构的领导层确定关键干预措施、扩大基础设施并加强计划，以提高全国范围内对压缩天然气的采用。该声明称，政府将加大力度推广压缩天然气作为更廉价的交通替代燃料，并再次强调加快在全国部署100万辆燃气动力汽车。这一新的推动举措是在取消汽油补贴以来公众对公共交通成本持续上涨的担忧中提出的，这增加了商业运输运营商的燃料费用，并对家庭收入造成压力。联邦政府一直将压缩天然气作为汽油的替代品进行推广，因为它在能量等效基础上通常更便宜。然而，它能在多大程度上降低交通费用取决于加油站的可用性、负担得起的车辆改装、可靠的天然气供应以及运营商是否将燃料节省传递给乘客。埃克波表示，尼日利亚丰富的天然气储量提供了一个降低运输成本、增加国内天然气消耗并刺激经济增长的机会。“尼日利亚是一个天然气国家，天然气储量指数超过80年，这就是我们谈论天然气十年（或数十年）的原因，”他说。部长强调需要落实总统博拉·蒂努布通过压缩天然气使交通更负担得起的指令，并向官员们保证政府将继续提供支持。“重要的是我们要听取总统先生的指令，通过压缩天然气使交通更便宜。我们将继续给予你们所有支持，提供必要的援助，以确保我们将这个项目推进到合乎逻辑的结论，”埃克波说。他敦促总统压缩天然气和电动汽车倡议以及天然气十年秘书处持续投资于加油基础设施、车辆改装设施以及扩大天然气作为交通燃料使用的其他必要组成部分。埃克波还对总统压缩天然气和电动汽车倡议当前领导层下取得的进展表示欢迎，重申政府支持该计划的承诺。他进一步透露，国内天然气消耗量首次超过每天20亿立方英尺，称这一发展是一个深化天然气利用并推进国家经济雄心的机会。总统压缩天然气和电动汽车倡议主席伊斯梅尔·艾哈迈德表示，该倡议将加大投资和计划，以扩大加油基础设施并增加改装为燃气运行的车辆数量。艾哈迈德说，这一努力旨在使压缩天然气对运输运营商更易获取，并帮助降低数百万尼日利亚人的交通费用。他补充说，由天然气十年秘书处完成的一项联合行业市场研究为加速推广、监测进展、识别基础设施差距和改进实施提供了框架。据他介绍，该研究将帮助政府和行业利益相关者确定优先干预措施，并加强使压缩天然气作为交通燃料广泛可用的努力。

https://leadership.ng/presidency-denies-.summary_zh: 周日由总统府发布的声明中，博拉·蒂努布总统的信息和战略特别顾问巴约·奥纳努加敦促尼日利亚人无视这一说法，认为所涉金额与尼日利亚液化天然气公司历史上向联邦支付的股息不一致。然而，总统府驳斥了这一指控，坚持认为所声称的金额无法得到既定收入分享公式和尼日利亚液化天然气公司股息支付历史的支撑。
https://leadership.ng/presidency-denies-.body: In a statement issued by the State House on Sunday, the Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, urged Nigerians to disregard the claim, arguing that the amount involved was inconsistent with NLNG’s historical dividend payments to the Federation. Makinde had made the allegation on Friday at the 2027 Budget Stakeholders’ Consultative Engagement held at the Olola Ogunlana Hall, International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan. The governor reportedly said the states were each entitled to ₦250 billion and that Oyo State had already identified projects that could expand its economy. He alleged that the funds would not be released until after the 2027 elections. “Each state was supposed to get ₦250 billion. We had already identified projects that would expand Oyo State’s economy. But they have now said the money will not be paid until after the election. Is the election more important than the people of Nigeria?” Makinde was quoted as saying. However, the Presidency rejected the allegation, insisting that the amount claimed could not be supported by the established revenue-sharing formula and NLNG’s dividend payment history. According to Onanuga, distributing ₦250 billion to each of the 36 states would amount to ₦9 trillion, excluding the federal government, the Federal Capital Territory and the 774 local government areas. The statement explained that, under the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) revenue-sharing formula, states receive 26.72 per cent of distributable Federation Account revenue. It argued that for the 36 states alone to receive a combined ₦9 trillion from NLNG dividends, the company would have to declare more than ₦33.68 trillion, equivalent to about $25 billion, in a single payout. The Presidency maintained that NLNG had never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single declaration. “NLNG has paid approximately $21.5 billion in dividends to the Federation over the last 25 years, with less than $3 billion realised since President Bola Ahmed Tinubu assumed office,” the statement said. It added that the claim of a single dividend payment exceeding the company’s entire reported lifetime distribution to the Federation was inconsistent with the figures cited by the government. The Presidency also criticised Makinde’s public statements since he declared his presidential ambition, accusing him of making misleading claims. It recalled his previous description of the financial allocations states receive from the Federation Account, including Oyo State, as “voodoo.” While acknowledging the governor’s constitutional right to pursue his presidential ambition, the statement urged him to avoid making claims it described as false and misleading. “We urge the public to disregard these unfounded claims, which serve only to mislead citizens and stoke needless disaffection against the Federal authorities,” it said. In July, the company’s Chief Executive Officer, Adeleye Falade, said NLNG had paid $47.2 billion in dividends to all its shareholders, including the Federal Government, from revenue of $149.6 billion since it began operations. NLNG’s Facts and Figures report also showed that annual payments to the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, its government shareholder, stood at $1.39 billion in 2014, $722.44 million in 2021 and $1.10 billion in 2022. Meanwhile, the 36 states reportedly received ₦4.83 trillion from the Federation Account between January and June, with Oyo State receiving ₦147.32 billion. Makinde declared his presidential ambition on May 14 at a rally in Ibadan under the APM, following the party’s alliance with a faction of the Peoples Democratic Party led by Kabiru Turaki.
